articleTitle: Gen5 CEM RX Compliance Simulation Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The PCIe Gen5 CEM RX compliance test presents significant challenges compared to traditional electrical margin tests for marginal systems due to the injection of additional jitter and noise during the RX compliance testing process. Currently, there exists a notable gap in standardized PCIeGen5 CEM RX compliance simulation methodologies available to system designers for evaluating platform design risks prior to PCB board fabrication or system builds. This deficiency often results in costly system board redesigns when RX compliance tests fail in validation stage. This study introduces a new PCIe Gen5 CEM RX compliance simulation methodology that addresses this critical issue. The proposed approach enables system designers to evaluate whether a platform design meets CEM RX compliance standards before PCB board tape-out (TO). By implementing this methodology, designers can conduct comprehensive risk assessments of their designs through RX compliance simulations. The advantage of the proposed RX compliance simulation methodology is its potential to yield substantial cost savings for product development and accelerate time-to-market for product launches. By shift-left identifying and mitigating compliance issues early in the design stage, this methodology offers a proactive approach to ensuring design validity and reducing redesign times.

articleTitle: Investigating Human Mental Workload During Human Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study investigates human mental workload during Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC). The experiment involved fifteen healthy male subjects who collaborated with a robotic arm in three different task conditions: human-robot (HR) collaboration, human-human (HH) collaboration, and human working alone (H). The mental workload was quantified using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to measure prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation and NASA-TLX questionnaires. Results indicated that HR collaboration required less mental workload than the other two conditions, with increased task stability and reduced physical effort. This highlights the potential of HRC to optimize task performance by reducing human mental and physical strain. Additionally, in the context of the panel industry, where the assembly and handling of panels are critical tasks, HRC offers a promising solution to address the challenges posed by an aging workforce and reduced labor availability. By improving manufacturing efficiency and flexibility, HRC can significantly enhance the overall productivity of panel production processes.

articleTitle: Optimizing Low-Temperature Polymer Thermo Compression Bonding and Polymer Patterning for 3D Multi-Chip Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study presents foundational research results for Cu/polymer hybrid bonding technology, which is essential for the miniaturization, low power consumption, and high-performance semiconductor manufacturing in the AI era. To overcome the limitations of Cu-Cu hybrid bonding using conventional SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> dielectrics, we explored low-temperature polymer thermo-compression bonding (TCB) and patterning methods through dry etching of polymer thin films. High purity pV3D3 thin films were deposited using the iCVD process, followed by FTIR, XPS, and AFM analyses after various surface treatment processes. Additionally, TCB results were presented through SAT and SEM analyses, and a bonding mechanism was proposed, focusing on the chemical structure changes during TCB. Furthermore, we present the polymer dry-etching results for the Cu damascene process in the Cu/polymer hybrid process. Ultimately, the potential for 3D multi-chip integration using Cu/polymer structures is demonstrated, contributing to advancements in 3D chip integration Technology.

articleTitle: Influence of Current Distribution Variations on Contact Resistance Measurement in Cu-Cu Bonding Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper evaluates the current distribution characteristics in the CBKR(Cross-Bridge-Kelvin-Resistor) structure and SGC (Stacked-Greek-Cross) structure designed to extract contact resistance occurring at the Cu-Cu bonding interfaces. We investigated a method to accurately extract contact resistance using Electromagnetic (EM) simulation. The current distribution varies depending on the thickness of the copper, the direction of current passing through the bonding interface, the interconnect size, and the imposed contact resistivity, which in turn affects the measurement of contact resistance. This result suggests a direction for more accurate measurement of contact resistance.

articleTitle: Advancements in Electroless Copper Plating for Via Shrinking Technology Trend
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The pursuit of smaller blind micro via size in IC substrate technology development is driven by the need for higher density integration, increased functionality, and improved performance of electronic devices. As via size shrinks and aspect ratio increases, it is inevitable to face challenges to maintain good copper via filling and reliability at via interconnect interface. Herein we demonstrate an electroless copper deposition of semi-additive process (SAP) fulfills both good reliability and throwing power for via diameter size ranging from 20 to 50 µm and dielectric thickness from 20 to 30 µm. One of the keys relies on the “accelerator” bath before panels enter electroless copper bath for electroless copper plating. In such bath, cleaner, antioxidant, wetting agent are included. The cleaner is used to remove copper oxide from the via bottom, ensuring the best possible copper surface quality before starting electroless copper plating. Antioxidant resides in the via can delay the oxidation of copper and simultaneously facilitate subsequent copper ion deposition in the same area. Wetting agent, though, helps these functional components penetrate the small via. This electroless copper deposition design enables throwing power of approximately 80% to be achieved in vias with a diameter of 20 µm and a depth of 20 µm. The copper grain exhibits good continuity at the electroless copper interface, with minimal voids, as observed under 30kx SEM cross-sectional inspection of vias with the same diameter and depth. Quick via pull reliability tests were also performed on the same vias, and no failures were found among 4000 tested vias. Other typical performance evaluation items for electroless copper, such as peel strength, electroless copper thickness and coverage, will not be compromised. In summary, electroless copper process is being investigated to address the new challenges associated with the technology trend of shrinking via sizes. We demonstrated an electroless copper product SAP8000 with an accelerator bath consisting of cleaner, antioxidant and wetting agents, which enhances throwing power and reliability performance.

articleTitle: New, Low Dk, ULTRA-LOW LOSS Substrate Material Offers Better Manufacturability
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: To offer design flexibility and improved performance for higher frequency signal, goals for development of a novel printed circuit material started with physical properties. In addition to low Dk and Df, features were incorporated to improve processing and permit more construction options for designs to reduce stack height. Innovation was focused on the interaction between conductor and dielectric. Changes to polymer resin chemistry and formulation are the means to a significant improvement in adhesion. Benefits are realized both where resin is acting as an adhesive, where excellent bond is achieved to very smooth copper foil products, with minimal bond enhancement treatment. Related improvements are found where higher polymer surface energy accepts metallization more readily (e.g., electroless copper) or enables prepreg and other adhesives to bond to exposed base dielectric. The paper focuses initially on physical properties and electrical performance. Key properties considered are dielectric constant (2.1 to 2.3, depending on product and construction) and ultra-low loss tangent (from 0.0005 to 0.0009). These values are optimized in design of the material set, as resin formulation accounts for dielectric properties and physical chemical functions which provide improved adhesion, enhance UV-Laser via formation and assure deposition of electroless copper or alternatives to provide an initial conductive path for plating vias.

articleTitle: Multi-stepped Solder Resist Patterning Technology for Advanced IC Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel process technology of solder resist (SR) thinning, RT system, to form multi-stepped structures. This study examines key parameters, such as temperature and immersion time of the process. By leveraging photolithography process, the RT system achieves highly uniform and selective SR thickness reduction that enables formation of unique SR structures. The study explores the demonstration of complex SR structures, such as SR dams with partial Cu pad exposure, and different types of SR opening structures in a single SR layer. Comparative analysis between the RT system and conventional development processes highlights the superior uniformity and process stability of the RT system in achieving tailored SR structures. Analysis and demonstration in this study indicates that the technology offers a unique and reliable process solution for the next generation of integrated circuit (IC) packaging industry.

articleTitle: Cu-Cu Bonding at 200°C Using a Copper Surface Treatment Solution that Activates the Copper Electrode Surface for Hybrid Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We have developed the treatment liquid that modifies the copper electrode surface to a copper-copper bondable state at a low temperature of 200°C. Copper nanoparticles are formed on the copper electrode surface by applying this liquid to the bonding surface of the copper electrode followed by heat treatment at < 200°C. This property has been utilized to achieve fine pitch copper-copper connections with a pitch of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Via Impedance Simulation and Control in PCB Manufacture for 112Gb/s
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As AI (Artificial Intelligence), cloud computing, and 5.5G technologies continue to advance, the demand for bandwidth has surpassed what 400G can provide. In response, the IEEE and OIF Standards Institute have developed and released protocol specifications for 800G and 112Gb/s, prompting service providers and CSPs (Cloud Service Providers) to turn to 800G products for launch and mass production. The design of the 800G employs a single-rate architecture operating at 112Gb/s Serdes, which imposes stringent signal integrity requirements across the entire PCB (Printed Circuit Board) link. To meet the tight impedance and insertion loss tolerances necessary for 112Gb/s design, PCBs incorporate sophisticated designs including the use of ultra-low-loss CCL (Copper Clad Laminate) with hybrid (FR-4) design, very low profile copper foil, low Dk (Dielectric Constant) and low Df (Dispersion Factor) glass fabric, as well as low etch and profile oxide treatments. However, managing transmission line impedance and insertion loss alone is insufficient for meeting the demands of 112Gb/s; via impedance must also be meticulously controlled to ensure impedance continuity throughout the link. The complexity of via structures presents challenges in measuring them using traditional TDR (Time Domain Reflectometer) and VNA (Vector Network Analyzer) equipment. Conventional via impedance simulation software is inadequate for accurate simulation for real PCB via design. To address this issue, the study utilizes three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation software to construct a differential pair model. The PCB Gerber file is imported and the actual via design including the BGA area and press fit is modeled. It investigates the impact of key PCB design elements such as different laminate dielectric constants (Dk), annular ring and anti-pad design, back drill stubs, and drill size selection. The simulation model is adjusted based on measured impedance data from the PCB to refine the impedance prediction model and make simulations that consider the influence of PCB manufacturing deviations on via impedance and insertion loss. Additionally, PCB control tolerance was established. The study demonstrates that after optimization, the via impedance can differ from the transmission line impedance by less than 5%, and the insertion loss can be improved by approximately 2%. This simulation model effectively aids in controlling via impedance, ensuring manageable insertion loss for PCB links, and holds promising applications in high-speed communication scenarios.

articleTitle: Electrical Characterization and Analysis of High-Speed Data Center Platforms Utilizing Diverse De-Embedding Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Over time, various methods have been developed to remove test fixture effects from printed circuit board (PCB) electrical tests to ensure accurate electrical characterization. This paper, the advanced de-embedding methodology with 2x - Thru is adopted that designers are empowered to perform channel risk assessments effectively, verifying PCB channel loss and system characteristic impedance early in the design process. This approach allows for the early detection of significant design issues enabling timely improvements to product quality.

articleTitle: Establish Deep Learning Model to Predict PCBA Reflow Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study reflow profile curve prediction of Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) by deep learning model establishment. The solder joints of all Surface Mount Technology (SMT) components are heated by the multiple top and bottom heating zones of convection reflow oven. In other words, the solder joints must be heated to reach the required temperature and enough time for full soldering process. Therefore, it is a challenge to simultaneously predict the temperatures in different zones with specific duration time in each zone. Especially focus on the high complexity of server PCBA profile prediction because of many thermocouples in SMT thermal profile board assembly. The solution is to simplify multiple profile curves as one average curve and define the key factors as the major features of deep learning model. Collect the product features and the production features to do the data processing. Adopt the algorithm: Multi-head Attention Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (MHA Bi-LSTM) to establish the deep learning model and achieve high accurate forecasting in reflow profiles of new product development stage. The Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values of these predicted profile curves are less than 10% to prove the deep learning model establishment of reflow profile prediction is feasible.

articleTitle: Experimental and Numerical Investigation on Dynamic Response of Flip Chip Package Under Board Level Drop Test
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The demand for the market is tend to be multiple functional, light weight, and miniaturized volume for portable and wearable electronic devices. The portable device would suffer from various situations or external forces leading to failure during the daily environment. The most common accident is the device falls to a rigid surface contributing to the failure of solder inside the device. Therefore, the dynamic response of the flip chip package under board level drop test is presented with the experimental and numerical analysis. The dynamic response of bare PCB is measured with the mounted gauge strain on the PCB. The numerical analysis of explicit and implicit finite element methods are both proposed and validated with experiment. The modal analysis is also presented and shows the identical frequency of modal between experiment and finite element analysis. The explicit and implicit finite element method for drop test is discussed on the estimated different behavior for the PCB. The flip chip package is further considered after the finite element method is validated for the numerical analysis. The several parameters of flip chip package and PCB are discussed to improve the dynamic response of solder during the drop test.

articleTitle: Reduction of Permanganate Treatment Time in Wet Desmearing Process Using Vacuum Ultraviolet Irradiation from Excimer Lamp
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As electronic devices continue to become more compact and sophisticated, there is a growing demand for high-density printed circuit boards (PCBs) capable of accommodating densely mounted narrow-pitch and high-pin-count packages. These high-density PCBs are manufactured using the build-up method, which involves alternating multiple insulation layers (typically, epoxy resin with silica fillers) and wiring layers (electrolytic copper plating) onto a core material (typically, copper-clad laminate; CCL). The wiring layers are formed using a semi-additive process (SAP), and blind via holes are formed in the insulation layers by laser processing and then filled with electrolytic copper plating to establish electrical connections between wiring layers. However, a residue called smear, composed of pyrolytic carbon and silica fillers because of the thermal transformation of epoxy resin caused by the heat generated during laser processing, remains at the bottom of the via holes. Smear remaining at the bottom of the via holes during electrolytic copper plating leads to conductive failure between wiring layers, thereby the desmearing process aiming to remove smear is crucial in SAP.

articleTitle: Substantially Improved Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Performance of Gradient-Conductive Ti3C2 Tx MXene/Polyimide Composite Films
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Polymer-based conductive nanocomposites are promising candidates for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, which is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of electronic devices and protecting human health from electromagnetic radiation exposure. In this study, Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> T, MXene was incorporated for its electrical conductivity, while polyimide (PI) served as a protective matrix to prevent MXene oxidation, thus improving the composite's durability. A gradient-conductive Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> T <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> MXene/PI composite film was developed by systematically varying the concentrations of MXene and PI. The resulting gradient film exhibited superior EMI shielding performance, with a total shielding effectiveness (SET) averaging ~50.01 dB in the X-band frequency range (8-12.4 GHz). The absorption component (EMI SEA) dominated, reaching around 45.02 dB, while the reflection component (EMI SER) contributed minimally (~4.99 dB). The gradient-conductive structure, consisting of a less conductive top layer and a highly conductive bottom layer, facilitated effective absorption and reflection of electromagnetic waves, extending the dissipation path and enabling multiple internal reflections, thus minimizing secondary emissions. The composite demonstrated only a slight reduction (~4.67%) in its total EMI SET value (dropping to 47.66 dB) after being subjected to heat treatment at 150°C for three days under ambient conditions, indicating good thermal stability. This work presents a straightforward and cost-effective method for fabricating high-performance and sustainable EMI shielding materials, making them suitable for applications in wearable electronics and aerospace technology.

articleTitle: NiPdAu top Metal for Clip and Cu/Au Wire Bonding in a Hybrid Package
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Electroless plated metal, such as electroless nickel electroless palladium immersion gold (ENEPIG Ni/Pd/Au) [1], [2] is a promising candidate for solder-based device interconnects. As it only deposits on the metal pads, it can be used for packages having both clip and wire bonding. This study focuses on evaluating the manufacturability and reliability of NiPdAu plating in the power device package that enables both clip and wire integration. These devices were observed to be capable of meeting the reliability requirements of the consumer mission profile. As a result, this investigative approach is beneficial for the risk evaluation of NiPdAu plating in these packages.

articleTitle: The Improvement of Cu/PI Hybrid Bonding by Low-Wave Length Ultraviolet Light Pretreatment
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the advent of the post-Moore era, the size reduction transistors has encountered the limitations of semiconductor physics. Advanced packaging technology such as 3D IC and heterogeneous integration are developing to overcome those problems. With respect to hetergeneous integration, hybrid bonding plays an important role and Cu/polymer bonding has begun to attract attention. In this study, UV-C light source with specific wavelength of 220 nm was used to pretreat the faying surface for strengthening the Cu/Cu and PI/PI bonding respectively. The results show that a proper light expoure effectively increased the joint strength. FTIR analysis confirms that it was related to the hydroxyl ligands formed on the surface.

articleTitle: Fracture Analysis of Micro-vias with Low to High Void Existence at Electroless Cu Plated Layers after Thermal Shock Reliability Cycle Test
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The electronics manufacturing industry is demanding higher microvia densities and smaller microvia diameters. This is to achieve multi-functional yet compact devices. However, the downsizing movement would make the weak microvia (WMV) problem obvious, as thinner and smaller designs physically reduce the strength and durability of the devices. WMV cracks have been found primarily at the bottom of the microvia where the electroless copper plating layer is located. In our presentation at IMPACT 2023[1], the reliability of 3-layer double-sided packaging substrates with varying degrees of void presence in their electroless copper plated layers of 60 micron microvias was estimated by a -55°C x 15 min/150°C x 15 min thermal shock reliability cycle test. Reliability was estimated using the Weibull analysis method by the number of failed thermal shock cycles when the internal circuit broke. As a result, the package substrate with more voids in the electroless Cu plated layer was found to have lower reliability in the thermal shock cycle test (F(10%)=app. 500 cycles) than the package substrate with fewer voids in the electroless copper plated layer (F(10%) = app. 1000 cycles). In addition, strain concentrations in the microvia bottom areas where the electroless copper plated layers are located were confirmed by the finite element method simulation due to the discrepancies of the layered materials. The strain concentration is more obvious in the micro vias near the core layer of the packaging substrates.

articleTitle: Applying Hybrid Numerical Simulation of Capillary Underfill Flow to Advanced Packaging Technologies in Fine Pitch Multi-Chip Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Traditional methods of studying the influence of various process parameters on underfill flow behavior, such as the dispensing pass location, drop mass, and the order and waiting time between dispensing passes, have required time-consuming and expensive experiments. Recognizing these limitations, 3D numerical simulation solving the Navier-Stokes equations has emerged as a viable alternative [1]. However, the increasing demand for a higher number of micro bumps and a diminishing gap between the chip and substrate necessitates a finer mesh to accurately resolve geometric features and simulate flow behavior determined by the distribution of micro bumps. Additionally, large multi-chip modules (MCMs) such as Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) often require significantly long processing times. These factors, however, come at the cost of significantly extended computational time.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of Thermal Performance on Fan Out POP Package
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The innovative advantages of advanced packaging bring unprecedented opportunities to an increasingly competitive market. In particular, the changes in appearance size and electrical advantages provide customers with high-quality solutions and support customers in realizing more efficient interconnection of everything. As 5G becomes mainstream, speed and efficiency greatly improve the quality of human life, so there is an increasing demand for complex applications that rely on ultra-low latency. Such as FO-PoP packaging structure is the most advanced vertically integrated integration technology. It also brings thermal performance request and have challenge when two packages stacking or memory start to dissipate heat. Following paper statement will simulation some circumstance to validate package performance before real product implementation. According to design on advanced silicon node wafer with package stacking on package and high power application which aims to high thermal package solution. This paper is to present thermal dissipation analysis of FO-PoP packaging. By using thermal simulation modeling to figure out factors for different die thickness circumstances. Through DOE to compare and explore different combinations with relative die thickness and high thermal DAF (die attach film) and compound is conducted to get optimum package architecture to measure theta Jc temperature, to conclude the best thermal performance.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches to Sustainable Manufacturing: Solvent-Free Copper Extraction And Zero Liquid Discharge Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The electronics manufacturing industry is under increasing pressure to adopt sustainable practices due to environmental concerns and stringent regulations. This abstract delves into the transformative potential of Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems in enhancing water quality and environmental sustainability in Integrated Circuit Substrate (ICS) and Printed Circuit Board (PCB) manufacturing. ZLD systems represent a critical advancement in wastewater management, aiming to eliminate liquid waste and promote water reuse. The implementation of ZLD in ICS manufacturing addresses significant challenges, including high water consumption and the discharge of metal-laden effluents. The ZLD process involves multiple stages: wastewater pretreatment, concentration, crystallization, separation, and final purification for reuse. This comprehensive treatment approach not only conserves water but also prevents environmental contamination by capturing and managing all solid and liquid waste. The necessity of ZLD systems is underscored by the increasing scarcity of freshwater resources and the high-water usage inherent in PCB and ICS production. Traditional manufacturing processes consume between 800 to 10,000 Liters of water per square meter of produced material. By adopting ZLD systems, manufacturers can significantly reduce their water footprint and comply with stringent environmental regulations, thus ensuring long-term viability and corporate social responsibility. The benefits of ZLD in industrial applications are manifold. Primarily, these systems contribute to substantial water conservation by treating and recycling wastewater, making it suitable for reuse in manufacturing processes. Additionally, ZLD systems enhance environmental protection by virtually eliminating liquid waste discharge, thereby mitigating the risk of pollution and contamination. They also help industries meet and exceed regulatory requirements related to wastewater discharge, thus avoiding potential penalties and fostering a positive environmental reputation. Case studies from existing ZLD installations in PCB manufacturing facilities demonstrate significant improvements in water quality and operational efficiency and will be explained in the paper. For example, existing installations systems have shown the capability to process up to 15 cubic meters of wastewater per hour, achieving high standards of water purity suitable for reuse. These systems are designed to handle the complex wastewater profiles typical of electronics manufacturing, including high concentrations of metals and chemicals. Complementing the ZLD discussion, the potential for solvent-free copper extraction in PCB manufacturing is noteworthy. Traditional liquid-liquid extraction methods, which are hazardous and costly, can be replaced with ion-exchange resin technology. This method not only reduces environmental hazards but also enhances the economic efficiency of copper recovery processes. Experimental studies have demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of ion-exchange resins in removing and recovering copper from etching solutions, providing a sustainable alternative to conventional methods. In conclusion, the integration of Zero Liquid Discharge systems in ICS and PCB manufacturing is a pivotal step towards achieving environmental sustainability and regulatory compliance in the electronics industry. These systems offer a viable solution to the dual challenges of water scarcity and pollution, while the concurrent development of solvent-free copper extraction technologies further underscores the industry's commitment to sustainable practices. As these technologies continue to evolve, they hold the promise of significantly reducing the environmental footprint of electronics manufacturing, paving the way for a greener future.

articleTitle: The Impact of Recent Revision of Enepig Specification - Ipc 4556a
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The 4-14F IPC Standards Committee are close to finalizing (at the time of writing) a revision to the IPC 4556 specification for Electroless Nickel/Electroless Palladium/Immersion Gold (ENEPIG) finished Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs). Revision A brings a more comprehensive evaluation of metal layer thickness measurements, compositions, and introduces a quality aspect for nickel corrosion following a successful publication of the revised IPC 4552B (ENIG specification). The introduction of these revisions will ensure a higher level of quality for conforming ENEPIG deposits, but it will also present some challenges in achieving and consistently delivering the required level of quality from PCB fabrication. IPC 4556A will require the PCB fabricator to demonstrate capability in measuring and maintaining electroless nickel, palladium, and gold thicknesses, electroless nickel %P composition, along with conformance to a newly introduced corrosion specification. IPC 4556A covers traditional ENEPIG using immersion gold technology and introduces a newer gold plating technology - reduction assisted gold (also known as hybrid or semi-autocatalytic gold). In short, the fabricator has more work to ensure an IPC 4556A compliant ENEPIG deposit. This paper will provide a comprehensive review of IPC 4556A, supplying explanations and examples of conforming and non-conforming ENEPIG to help the fabricator understand and embrace the challenges posed by the new specification and provide a higher quality ENEPIG deposit.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models with Synthetic Minority Oversampling in Predicting Substrate Warpage (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The performance of semiconductors is improved through advanced packaging design, and it is necessary to accurately calculate the specific values of the thermal and mechanical properties of semiconductor packages. For packaging structures, uneven warping often occurs on the packaging surface when the temperature changes. Packaging warpage is typically obtained through measurement characterization. Therefore, the impact of the volume and design of each material in the package on thermal effects becomes critical. This study employs machine learning (ML) models, namely Support Vector Regression, LightGBM, Random Forest and eXtreme Gradient Boosting, to forecast substrate warpage at both room temperature and high temperature. The input data include design parameters such as substrate thickness, die size, die thickness, core thickness, package size, and heat sink thickness. In addition, the synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) is used to deal with imbalanced data in this study. The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) is used as a measurement for evaluating performances of machine learning models. Numerical results reveal that four machine learning models can obtain satisfied forecasting results and the eXtreme Gradient Boosting model generates the most accurate outcomes. Thus, machine learning models are feasible and promising alternative in forecasting substrate warpage.

articleTitle: Green Technology - Enabling Productivity and Sustainability for IC Substrate Manufacturing (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Often “Green” technologies, while advantageous for the environment, come with disadvantages to existing manufacturing processes. Sometimes this means taking a loss on productivity and sometimes entails higher cost overall. However, at times technologies can represent a major shift in manufacturing paradigms and actually offer significant improvements along with general benefits to reducing a manufacturer's total carbon footprint. In this paper, we will explore such an example in the form of laser via drilling for IC Substrate (Flip-Chip Ball Grid Array). We'll review the technological enablers behind an AOD-based (Acousto-Optical Device) CO2 laser drilling system that reduce power consumption and utilities footprint (space, water consumption), while increasing productivity and lowering CO2 emissions, as well as running costs. We'll address the “green” benefits (lower carbon footprint) of embracing new, innovative technology and explore some “roadmap” advantages of introducing AOD-based laser processing to substrate applications development.

articleTitle: Flux-Less Solder Ball Attachment Technology (FLAT) for Advanced BGA Assembly
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Mass reflow soldering technology using flux have been widely adopted in semiconductor assembly process for decades, particularly in ball grid array (BGA) solder ball attachment process. However, advanced semiconductor packages are now facing interconnect scaling down to sub-micron levels, with the pitches of both bumps and BGAs becoming increasingly finer. Simultaneously, dies are becoming larger and thinner, while PCB boards are also increasing in size and becoming thinner. These changes have made it a significant challenge to control flux residue and die/PCB board warpage, which can impact reliability after mass reflow soldering.

articleTitle: Advanced Lithography Solutions to Address Extreme Die Shifts in Fan-Out Panel-Level Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) is among the most effective solutions for meeting the demands of 2.5D packaging while also reducing costs. Nevertheless, FOPLP encounters several critical process challenges. A primary issue is die shifting, which arises from the reconstitution process in die-first FOPLP. These complications lead to the displacement of dies from their intended positions. If die shifting is not adequately recognized and addressed during the lithography process, it can cause substantial overlay errors and significantly reduce overlay yield. To address the challenges of die shifting, a novel lithography solution has been proposed: outlier control technology integrated with feedforward lithography. This advanced technique involves a site-by-site (SBS) correction method facilitated by an algorithm that identifies outliers on the substrate. The algorithm optimizes overlay corrections to eliminate the side effects of these outliers, thereby ensuring high overlay yield. Moreover, feedforward lithography mitigates the impact on throughput caused by the time-intensive SBS corrections required by outlier control technology. In this study, we will examine the impact of die shifting on overlay yield in FOPLP and explore how outlier control technology combined with feedforward lithography addresses the associated yield and throughput challenges. We will demonstrate the application of these technologies on a test vehicle, a 510mm x 515mm panel containing 400 dies, with some dies intentionally displaced from their nominal positions. The test vehicle will be processed using advanced outlier control technology in conjunction with feedforward lithography. This demonstration will illustrate the integration of these technologies and how this strategy effectively addresses the identified challenges. Additionally, we will review the demonstration results and discuss the advantages of this integrated approach.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Signal Integrity and Cost Efficiency in High Speed Serdes: Via-in-Pad vs. Non Via-in-Pad PCB Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study explores the impact of PCB design methodologies on signal integrity, performance, and cost in PCIe Gen6 applications. It compares via-in-pad and non via-in-pad designs, showing that optimized non via-in-pad designs can achieve similar performance to via-in-pad designs while offering cost benefits. Using electromagnetic simulations and empirical tests, the research assesses insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk, and economic factors such as manufacturing complexity and material costs. Findings suggest that well-optimized non via-in-pad designs provide comparable performance and reduced manufacturing costs. Recommendations are offered for optimizing non via-in-pad designs to balance high-speed data transmission with economic efficiency in next-generation computing systems.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Analysis of UCIe Channel in FOCoS Advanced Package
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In chiplet integration applications, various chips from different vendors can be integrated into one package structure using the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard. Fan-Out Chip on Substrate (FOCoS) is a promising advanced package that can achieve high channel density and high bandwidth. However, crosstalk in high-speed signals is a major factor impacting signal integrity. To effectively mitigate coupling noise between fine lines, an optimized signal-to-ground trace layout is essential. The design process outlined in this paper not only significantly reduces design cycle time but also addresses transmission loss and crosstalk effects in the die-to-die (D2D) area, thereby evaluating interconnect routing capabilities to meet UCIe x32 and x64 specifications.

articleTitle: Utilization of Au Passivation Nanolayer for Low-Temperature Cu-to-Cu Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The performance and functionality of semiconductor devices have so far continued to require higher levels as IT technologies progressively develop. Accordingly, the importance of back-end process of semiconductor process is increasing, and in particular, packaging technologies are being studies in various ways. Cu(copper)/dielectric hybrid bonding is one of the important technologies for heterogeneous integration in 3D packaging, and many studies for low-temperatures hybrid bonding have been conducted. In this study, low-temperature Cu bonding using Au(gold) passivation nanolayer was analyzed. The diffusion rate between Cu and Au deposited by an e-beam evaporator and sputter showed the opposite trends. W2W(wafer-to-wafer) and C2C(chip-to-chip) bonding and annealing were carried out at 180°C and 200 °C, respectively. A comparison of the bonding interface results was made based on the deposition methods of Au, as well as the differences in Au thickness. Bonding interface was analyzed using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Shear strength and resistance measurements were carried out to evaluate the bonding strength and electrical characteristics.

articleTitle: Efficient Management of High-Volume PCB Manufacturing Through Statistical In-board Characterization Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Intel® Automatic In-board Characterization (AIBC) has been created to enable comprehensive in-board characterization on a single board, facilitating the assessment of design quality, manufacturing variations, and PCB technology verification. [1]–[2] This study utilizes data obtained from AIBC measurements to perform statistical analysis, monitoring the quality of mass production. Process Capability Index (PCI) is a statistical measure of a process's ability to produce output within specified limits. It is used in the field of quality control to assess the capability of a manufacturing process, ensuring it meets certain performance standards. Therefore, this paper aims to analyze the quality of PCB manufacturing processes through the statistical indicator PCI.

articleTitle: Waving Warpage Goodbye: UV for Fan-Out
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)

articleTitle: Comparison of Through-Thickness Damage Distributions in Sheets in Bending under Tension Predicted by Several Empirical Ductile Fracture Criteria
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper develops a method for calculating the throughthickness distribution of damage parameters in plane-strain bending under tension, employing uncoupled damage mechanics models. The material is supposed to be elastic/plastic, strain hardening. No restrictions are imposed on the strain hardening law. Also, no restriction is imposed on the damage evolution law. The solution is facilitated by using a Lagrangian coordinate system. Specific calculations are provided for several widely used damage evolution laws. The solution found can be used to identify damage evolution laws with no finite element analysis, which is a great advantage for the damage evolution laws involving several constitutive parameters.

articleTitle: A Study of Efficiency of Total Volume of Mold Resin for Warpage in COW Process
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We have studied the warpage trends as a function of the total volume of mold resin in the Chip-on-Wafer (COW) process. By using face-down die bonding onto a waffle Si wafer, the remaining mold resin is reduced due to the structure of the waffle wafer and the additional thinning capability provided by face-down die bonding. This method results in a one-fourth reduction in warpage compared to the conventional face-up die bonding onto the bare Si wafer. This paper describes the changes in warpage throughout the COW and molding processes, both bare wafer and waffle wafer, and highlights the advantages of face-down die bonding.

articleTitle: Bubbling Matters?
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The rising of AI Servers trend to consume more power with the increasing heat dissipation as a major challenge in coming decade. To solve this very hot AI infrastructure problem the cooling systems evolve from air cooling to liquid cooling and phase change cooling. The immersion cooling is one of the most prominent cooling technologies that can solve this increasing heat dissipation problem with many know advantages. Despite of the advantages of immersion cooling with either single-phase or two-phase cooling liquids. The low boiling point characteristic of two-phase cooling liquids bubbling the fluids around the heat dissipation area that interest us on the possible and potential bubbling impacts on the localized areas' signals. In this paper, the design of experiment method will be introduced to assess and quantify the bubbling impact on the localized areas' signals with experimental data as well.

articleTitle: Pre-fabricated Via Array Substrate for Programmable AIoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: A pre-fabricated via array substrate and the customized redistribution traces are designed to provide small-volume large-variety production packaging producibility evaluation. The pre-fabricated via array substrate was composed of three-metal level copper redistribution layers and 200 μm height copper post. An active switch die was embedded in the copper post, it can programmable and modulate the signal transmission between integrated heterogeneous chips. We demonstrate a high-functionality package that interconnects multiple chips (Bluetooth, flash memory, and microcontroller unit) into a single system using simple 2P1M customized redistribution traces, reducing the complexity of layout design and increasing routing flexibility. It can be a cost-effective packaging, customized redistribution traces process in a short cycle time using existing via array substrate. The proposed pre-fabricated via array substrate and the customized redistribution traces for fan-out wafer-level packaging are expected to be a promising solution for high-performance system-in-package architectures. Advanced pre-fabricated via array substrate can guarantee the manufacturing yield, shortening the time-to-market, and reducing the production cost.

articleTitle: A Fracture Mechanics Model for Interface Debonding in 2.5-D Package under Solder Reflow
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this paper, a fracture mechanics model for the driving force of the debonding of Si sidewall-underfill interface in a fan-out (FO) chiplet package under solder reflow condition is presented. The numerical finite element (FE) based model considers the coupled hygro-thermo-mechanical response of the chiplet package under moisture sensitivity level (MSL) test condition. The model simulates the transient moisture diffusion and the subsequent vapor pressure development in the polymeric materials, and then evaluates the related hygroscopic and thermomechanical stresses in the package. In addition, the fracture mechanics parameters for the interface debond including the strain energy release rate and the phase angle are obtained from a 3-D virtual crack closure procedure. From the simulation results for a FO two-die package, it was shown that the primary debond driving forces of the Si-underfill interface at elevated temperatures are the CTE-mismatch related thermal stress and the crack-face vapor pressure. On the other hand, the moisture swelling does not contribute much to the debond growth. The estimated debond driving force would exceed the moisture-weakened fracture toughness of the interface if the defect size reaches a certain threshold. In addition to the comprehensive procedure that models the coupled hygro-thermo-mechanical driving force for interface debond growth at reflow temperature, a simplified model for evaluating the debonding risk was also presented. The simplified model ignores the transient moisture diffusion process and adopts an equivalent coefficient of thermal expansion for considering both thermal and moisture effects. By comparing to the results of the comprehensive model, it was shown that the simplified model is feasible as a first-order evaluation of the crack driving force under reflow condition.

articleTitle: Utilizing Both Backplane and Cable Connections in Server Systems: Viability and Challenges in a Common AI Server Design
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Following the introduction of the DC-MHS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> (Data Center Modular Hardware System) and AI (Artificial Intelligence) servers, the adoption of cabling topologies has become increasingly prevalent and indispensable. Within DC-MHS design, the Host Process Module (HPM) necessitates cabling for inter-module connectivity. In AI servers, components such as the HPM, PCI Express (PCIe) switch board, and UBB (Universal Baseboard) may not reside on the same chassis floor, necessitating vertical connections either through traditional backplane design or cables to link boards and modules. These connections are critical for high-speed signal transmission, exemplified by technologies like PCIe 5.0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> operating at 32 GT/s. Driven by escalating computing demands, the industry is eagerly anticipating PCIe 6.0 and exploring advancements towards PCIe 7.0, which runs at 64 GT/s and 128 GT/s respectively. This paper presents a generalized connection topology for HPM, PCIe switch board, and UBB. Simulation and measurement results are included to elucidate common challenges encountered in cabling topologies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Printed Circuit Board (PCB) Electrical Characteristics under Immersion Cooling Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In recent years, as power consumption in data centers has escalated, immersion cooling technology has garnered increasing attention due to its potential to significantly enhance cooling efficiency across various application scenarios. Liquids, which exhibit higher thermal conductivity compared to air, enable systems to more effectively dissipate heat from sources, thereby lowering the ambient temperature. Additionally, immersion cooling systems can distribute heat more uniformly, helping to minimize the formation of hot spots. This uniform heat distribution is particularly crucial for various system components, especially high-speed interconnected PCBs [1]. This research primarily focuses on comparing the ambient temperatures of PCBs under immersion cooling conditions with those of PCBs under traditional air cooling, aiming to enhance the electrical characteristics of PCBs and improve system channel design in immersion cooling environments.

articleTitle: A Study of a Plating Hanger for a Vertical Copper Electroplating Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Semiconductor technology plays a crucial role in the advancement of technology. The creation of powerful microchips has made our lives easier by automating tasks, improving communication, and providing access to vast arrays of information. Industries are being transformed through automation and digital innovation. This creates new opportunities and challenges along the way. Semiconductor manufacturers are becoming smarter by constantly improving the processes by which they manufacture and produce these microchips. One effective strategy to increase production and maximize efficiency is to ensure that these machines are regularly maintained and are constantly improved to guarantee the quality and quantity of the products. During the deposition process, the vertical continuous copper electroplating machinery runs nonstop to meet the demands of the manufacturing company. Due to continuous usage, the copper plating hanger's mechanical components encounter unavoidable deformation due to stress and strain, which causes the hanger's components to be misaligned and damaged. In this study, the researcher has redesigned the mechanical components of a copper plating hanger used in vertical continuous copper electroplating machinery, which is a critical piece of machinery utilized in semiconductor manufacturing. The copper plating hanger has three main critical mechanical components, namely the brass conductor, the stainless-steel horizontal bar, and the stainless-steel insulating clips. These components encounter the greatest deformation during continuous usage in the production line, which becomes damaged and unsalvageable after several usages during production; therefore, it is inefficient, unsustainable, and not cost-worthy. Actual mechanical design experiments were conducted to compare the standardized fixed measurements of the copper plating hanger before and after it was used in the production line. The gathered data was used to analyze the misalignments that have occurred after being utilized in the production line. Thereafter, simulations through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) were performed to understand the stress, strain, and displacement behaviors of these components under different parameters and boundary conditions used in the actual design experiments. Comparing results of the aforesaid experiment yielded better design results. Such is useful to develop a more effective and efficient mechanical design. Therefore, design improvements were made for the copper plating hanger following the mechanical design principles from the mechanical engineering discipline. Design improvements were made through the fabrication of newly designed components such as the conductor guide for the brass conductor, the middle bracket for the stainless-steel horizontal bar, and the flange guide for the stainless-steel insulating clips. These newly designed components will improve the stability, precision, and accuracy of the copper plating hanger's three main critical mechanical components, as well as the overall precision of the copper plating hanger, which will contribute to the overall efficiency of the vertical continuous copper electroplating machinery.

articleTitle: Multi-Camera System with Advanced Image Correction Techniques for Industrial Applications (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study proposes a novel multi-camera calibration method specifically designed for industrial PCB (Printed Circuit Board) applications. The proposed method utilizes small targets to calibrate large industrial objects without requiring overlapping camera fields of view. It employs triangulation and other techniques to determine camera poses from partial images captured by the cameras. Image reconstruction techniques are then used to verify the camera poses. This approach does not necessitate additional sensors or projection equipment. Instead, it utilizes simulation software to set precise parameters, effectively reducing calibration errors and sensitivity. The method offers several advantages, including high accuracy, low cost, and simple structure, making it suitable for on-site camera calibration. By integrating this innovative multi-camera calibration method, the system provides a reliable and efficient solution for the precise calibration of cameras in PCB manufacturing and inspection processes. This enhances the overall quality control an d accuracy in the production of PCBs, ensuring high standards in the final product. Multi-camera systems hold significant importance in current industrial applications, particularly for scene reconstruction and camera pose estimation, which remain popular research topics. However, measuring large workpieces continues to be challenging. Our method offers an integrated approach using both virtual and real environments to estimate camera poses even when multiple cameras have non-overlapping fields of view (FOV).

articleTitle: Ultra Thinning Wafer Structures with Controllable Backside Etch Stop Layer for HBM and BSPDN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Wafer thinning is pivotal in the semiconductor packaging industry, particularly for advanced packaging technologies like High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and Backside Power Distribution Network (BSPDN). This study explores a novel wafer thinning technique combining single ion implantation and rapid thermal annealing. Specifically, boron ion implantation followed by annealing at 1000°C for 300 seconds was employed to define backside etch stop layers. Wet etching with a solvent mix of 23.4% KOH and 13.3% IPA at 70°C resulted in etch rates of 7.600 nm/s for bare silicon and 0.027 nm/s for boron-doped silicon, achieving a selectivity of 281. Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) were used to assess ion concentration and surface roughness, with TEM, SEM and FIB providing precise layer thickness measurements. This method offers enhanced control over wafer thinning, advancing the development of thinner, high-performance semiconductor devices tailored for future technological demands.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Double Pulse Tests for Si IGBT/SiC MOSFET Hybrid Switch Power Module Applied to Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In motor drives applied to electric vehicles, the inverter carries a high current due to the power rating. To increase current toleration, the power switches are paralleled in the inverter. Furthermore, the SiC MOSFET is implemented to achieve high switching speed and high efficiency. However, the high cost of SiC MOSFET leads to the high cost of the inverter, SiC MOSFET also has higher conduction losses than Si IGBT at full load. In this paper, the hybrid switch power module composed of one SiC MOSFET and one Si IGBT are proposed to reduce the cost and combine the advantages of both elements. The Double Pulse Test (DPT) simulation via LTspice is conducted to obtain turn-on and turn-off losses of the hybrid switch power module in different switching patterns.

articleTitle: Development of Polymer Base Hybrid Bonding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We have developed a hybrid bonding process that uses low-temperature curable polyimide to bond silicon chips with minimal damage. We designed a low elasticity photosensitive polyimide and a low-CTE polyimide for the hybrid bonding. As a result, we found that the elastic modulus at the temperature of bonding and the surface activation treatment affected the adhesiveness. It is thought that the plasma activation treatment increases the number of hydrophilic groups on the polyimide surface, and hydrogen bods are induced between the polyimide surfaces during low temperature bonding. Then, subsequent post annealing treatment causes a chemical reaction to bond polyimide surface. Furthermore, polishing conditions that could expose approximately 1-10nm of copper using CMP processes on a silicon wafer which formed Cu pad and polyimide. As a result, polyimide-polyimide and polyimide-Cu void free hybrid bonding processes are confirmed below 250°C.

articleTitle: Impact of Half-ounce Copper Foil Impact on PCB Electrical Characteristics in High-Layer Count Designs for High-Speed Data Center AI Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Copper thickness significantly influences board thickness and plays a crucial role in its design. While the thickness of copper in power/ground layers is generally fixed due to the requirements of power and current delivery requirements, this limitation does not apply to signal layers. In typical stack-up configurations, signal layers usually are about 1.2 mils in thickness, corresponding to one-ounce (oz) of copper. However, an alternative exists for signal layers: opting for half-ounce (0.5 Oz) copper, which is approximately 0.6 mils thickness. This choice can effectively reduce the overall board thickness by 0.6 mils for each signal layer, presenting a viable solution to manage and optimize board thickness constraints.

articleTitle: Analysis of Noise Coupling from 48V Voltage Regulator Common Module (VRCM) to High Speed I/O Traces
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The demand for 48V power solutions in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) has shown geometric growth. However, there is very little research on High-speed I/O signal traces for 48V servers. To study 48V noise coupling, this article analyzes the 48V noise coupling mechanism of a VRCM-based 48V Native power server system. A comparative analysis has also been conducted with traditional 12V server noise coupling to elucidate the differences. On this basis, conclusions are drawn, and corresponding suggestions are made for the design of 48V servers.

articleTitle: Effect of Plating Temperature on the Crystallization and Texture Development of Highly (111) Oriented Electroless Cu Nanotwins
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study achieved a significant milestone by fabricating a highly (111) textured electroless nanotwinned Cu (nt-Cu) film in columnar grains with specific additives in the electroless plating bath. Moreover, the study found that the plating temperature plays a crucial role in Cu nanotwins' crystallization and texture development. Even a 5-degree Celsius difference in plating temperature can significantly influence the twinning fraction, (111) texture development, and the formed twin coherency within the Cu film. The crystallization of (111) textured Cu nanotwins in columnar grains along the growth direction was much favored at a lower plating temperature of 40 °C. This lower temperature led to 88% of the deposited Cu nanotwins exhibiting a (111) textured orientation. This high percentage indicates a strong influence of the plating temperature on the texture development. Additionally, the electroless nanotwins deposited at 40 °C had higher coherency. The Cu film comprised up to 40% of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma 3$</tex> {111} of the total grain boundaries, indicating that the formed grains are organized in a more energy-stable lattice arrangement. The highly (111) textured and more coherent nanotwinned structure contributes to grain boundary strengthening, revealing the electroless nt-Cu film as a promising engineering material.

articleTitle: High Power Laser Sub-mount of DPC Ceramic for Edge Emitting Laser Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: High-power laser systems play a crucial role in industrial, scientific, and medical fields, where the stability of their performance directly impacts the reliability and efficiency of systems. The purpose of this research is to develop a novel high -power laser ceramic substrate by enhancing its thermal management, conductivity, and durability through the selection of suitable materials and precise manufacturing processes to meet the demands across various applications. The study utilized high thermal conductivity aluminum nitride ceramic substrates as the foundational material, achieving a thermal conductivity of 230 W/m.K, effectively dissipating heat and enhancing system thermal stability. In the metallization process, direct electroplating of copper technology is employed. Initially, copper electroplating is applied to the surface of the ceramic substrate, followed by electroplating with nickel gold on the copper surface. Alternatively, electroless immersion nickel/palladium/gold plating with additional electroless thick gold plating is utilized to ensure the conductivity and corrosion resistance of the metal layer. Subsequently, low-temperature annealing was conducted to further modify the crystal structure of the metal layers, thereby improving their stability, mechanical strength, and heat resistance. Finally, during the manufacturing process of evaporated gold-tin solder, photolithographic processes were employed to precisely control the shape and position of the solder, preventing solder overflow and ensuring the precision and reliability of laser chip bonding. The developed high-power laser ceramic substrate demonstrated outstanding performance after the manufacturing process. Firstly, the aluminum nitride ceramic substrate effectively enhanced the overall system's heat dissipation capability, thereby decreased heat accumulation and system temperature rise. The precise manufacturing and annealing processes of the metal layers ensured stability and durability under prolonged high-power operations while providing excellent electrical performance. The photolithographic process designed for solder shape and precise position control effectively prevented solder overflow during the manufacturing process, further ensuring reliable laser chip bonding and connection. This research successfully developed a high-power laser ceramic substrate, enhancing overall system performance and reliability through the precise design and optimization of materials, metallization processes, and solder manufacturing. Future research directions include further optimizing manufacturing processes to enhance product efficiency and cost-effectiveness to meet the growing demands of high-power laser applications.
