articleTitle: Optimization of High Aspect Ratio Through Glass Vias Void-Free Filling Using Complex System Response Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In advanced packaging field, 3-D integrated circuits have extensive applications in high-density interconnection (HDI) since component arrangement on 2-D planar wafer faces saturation. Through Glass Via (TGV) technology stands out due to its advantageous electrical, optical, and mechanical properties as a substrate. The main challenge in TGV filling is how to form electroplated copper bridge at the high aspect ratio (HAR) TGV midpoint such as, butterfly mode, X-shaped mode, and so on.[1] Periodic pulse reverse (PPR) plating technique is an effective method using in HAR through hole filling, due to advantageous concentration gradient and mass transport profile.[2] However, it is a challenge to find a quantitative output measure of the butterfly or X mode. The other challenge is that N levels for each P parameter in a P parameter pool form a huge N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sup> search space, which impedes to find the global optimal parameter-level combination.[3] To address this, we introduce AI Complex System Response (AI-CSR) platform, which offers insight into the system's response variations across the multidimensional parameter space.[4], [5] For a complex system having P parameters, the CSR function has coefficients. Only [(P2+3P+2)/2] «N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sup> calibration tests are needed to identify the system response, which allow us to identify the optimal parameter combinations and obtain the global maximum. The optimization target is represented by a quantitative system response property, E. This measure, E, is defined as a dimensionless group, translating a two-dimensional geometric requirement into a scalar quantitative output. This crucial step facilitates the application of the AI-CSR platform to achieve butterfly-shaped electroplating. The AI-CSR platform successfully identify the appropriate parameter-level combinations, achieving desired butterfly-mode plating with “I-shape” (Figure 1-a) as well as effectively preventing voids or seams formation during copper electroplating (Figure 1-b). The optimal P-N combination with the predicted highest output E=7.69 according to CSR is performed in confirmation experiment, yields an experimental E value of 7.37. This output makes the TGVs filling achieve bridging and start bottom-up filling within 1 hour and 20 minutes. Moving forward, our focus will be on further refining the P-N combination to attain the fastest TGV filling time without defects, ultimately further enhancing the production rate.

articleTitle: Multi-Device and Multi-Product Load Rate Analysis Tool Under Capital Expenditure
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The load rate analysis tool is used to explore the utilization of all equipment for production capacities of different products in this study, which is a kind of production capacity and equipment management tool to help companies in production planning and scheduling. In this study, the logic of the load rate analysis tool and its effectiveness on the company's production scheduling is illustrated with the BU's capital expenditure application. The load rate is planned and simulated through an algorithm to help companies develop the best production schedule. It can consider various factors, such as production scheduling days, working hours, equipment supply, etc., and adjust the production plan accordingly. Companies that use load rate analysis tools usually find it helps them to better manage the production process and reduce production costs.

articleTitle: Modular Edge Design and Thermal Mechanical Consideration for 5G vRAN and Edge AI
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Edge computing is becoming increasingly important due to the growth of 5G vRAN and Edge AI. However, the current state of edge designs and platforms is chaotic, with multiple different deployment locations and various specifications. To reduce the edge computing development costs and improve the scalability, a “modular edge design” is needed. The design should meet the infrastructure of operating environment requirements of edge computing and standardizes the building blocks to address the current design chaos. This paper introduces the concept of the Intel modular edge design (MED), which includes the edge modular building blocks such as (1) Intel Edge Host Processor Module (Intel Edge-HPM) (2) Edge Secure Control Module (Edge-SCM) (3) Modular Common Redundant Power Supply (M-CRPS) and other key components. Note that Intel modular edge design (MED) host processor module (HPM) specification effort is Intel proposed to what is required to achieve the common industry specification for edge specific designs, patterned after the recent OCP DC-MHS specifications. There will be four variant Intel edge-HPM board types (type A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$280\times 162.5\ \text{mm}$</tex>; type B <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$350\times 168\ \text{mm}$</tex>; type C <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$260\times 295\ \text{mm}$</tex> and type D <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$365\times 168\ \text{mm}$</tex>) for different form factors and market segments. And the detailed specification is planned to be presented and published at Open Compute Project (OCP) in Q4'2024. Moreover, this paper delivers the system design considerations for 5G vRAN and edge AI, which uses Intel edge-HPM type C as an example to compose of the 5G vRAN and edge AI solution with variant building blocks. It shows the feasibility and scalability of Intel modular edge design so that one HPM can be reusable and configurable to different products for variant market segments. Finally, Intel built the modular edge design proof of concept (POC) system and demonstrated that the building blocks of Intel modular edge design can fit within a 310mm short depth chassis. This paper will share the POC thermal mechanical limitation and the design considerations to address the thermal mechanical challenges of the edge computing. This modular edge design enables the industrial edge computing products to reduce development costs, increase flexibility, improve scalability, be compliant with NEBS and pave the way for a better future.

articleTitle: Using Uncertainty Analysis to Validate Reliability Prediction in WLP with Idealized Solder Joint Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The reliability of solder joints in semiconductor packaging is crucial as it significantly impacts the performance and reliability of electronic devices. The industry typically uses Accelerated Thermal Cycling Test (ATCT) tests to predict the lifetime of solder joints in packages. However, due to the high costs and lengthy time requirements of ATC tests, replacing traditional ATCT tests with finite element simulation is crucial. Simulation can improve design efficiency and further reduce time costs. Idealized solder joints are often used for modeling in simulation. However, real-world manufacturing processes introduce dimensional uncertainties, commonly referred to as tolerances, which affect the lifetime of solder joints. Therefore, uncertainty analysis is needed to validate the reliability analysis of using idealized solder joints for modeling. This research conducted an uncertainty analysis of solder joint dimensions to verify the effectiveness of using idealized solder joints for modeling and predicting the lifetime of solder joints under inherent manufacturing uncertainties. Specifically, for the wafer-level packaging (WLP) simulations, idealized solder joints were initially used for modeling, and the lifetime was predicted using the Coffin-Manson model. Uncertainty analysis was then performed with simulation, introducing variations in the upper pad diameter, lower pad diameter, and solder ball volume, resulting in 5 × 5 × 5, or 125 different geometric combinations of solder joints with manufacturing errors. The Coffin-Manson model was used again to predict the lifetimes of these solder joint combinations. A Weibull distribution analysis was conducted to determine the 63.2 percentile of the lifetime distribution under simulated manufacturing errors, also known as the characteristic life, which served as our standard metric for reliability evaluation. This characteristic life was then compared with the predicted lifetime from the idealized solder joint modeling to assess the reliability of the idealized modeling. The uncertainty analysis conducted in this research demonstrates that although manufacturing uncertainties lead to variations in the reliability of individual WLP reliability, the results from idealized solder joint modeling are very close to the overall characteristic life This result validates the robustness of using idealized solder joint modeling to simulate and predict WLP reliability, even in the presence of manufacturing uncertainties.

articleTitle: Warpage Optimization Design for FOPOP by Using Finite Element Analysis and Statistical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: A FOPOP (Fan out package on package) which adopts redistribution layer (RDL) technique to replace conventional substrate-based POP has benefits of thinner profile, better electrical and thermal performance. It has been used as high-end AP for smartphone in recent years. Wafer warpage control during wafer form fabrication process is important. Poor wafer warpage would impact the process pression adversely and even interrupt the process when exceeding wafer handling capacity of the machines. Moreover, package warpage is becoming more challenges due to thinner package thickness. Poor package warpage would affect quality results of SMT and stacking DRAM. Thus, the optimization of the material selection and design parameters becomes critical to the wafer and package warpage control. In this paper, Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation was performed to predict wafer and package warpage. Various structural parameters include RDL structure thickness, Cu stud height and die thickness were simulated. Then simulation results were analyzed by statistical analysis tool to identify critical parameters impacting package warpage. Moreover, warpage prediction formula was derived by performing the regressions analysis and best structural parameter combination also can be found out by statistical analysis tool. The FOPOP with the optimized package structure was assembled actually. Then its wafer warpage and package warpage were measured and compared with simulation results. Both results showed to be well agreement with simulation results. Hence, it showed that the package warpage could be optimized as early as in the design stage by FEA simulations with statistical analysis to shorten product development time and reduce development cost.

articleTitle: Electromigration Failure Study of Advanced Flip-chip QFN Solder Interconnects with Various Metallization Combinations for High-power Automobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this study, flip-chip quad flat no-lead (FCQFN) solder interconnects with various metallization combinations were investigated for the electromigration study. The effects of Ni and Ag metallizations on the interfacial reaction and electromigration failure behavior of the solder interconnects were investigated. Direct current input of 2 A (approximately 1.0 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) was applied to the solder interconnects at 160°C for a period achieving 200%-electrical-resistance-increase as a failure criterion. The additional incorporation of Ni metallization at the Cu pillar/Sn1.8Ag interface suppressed the growth of Cu-Sn IMCs at the interfaces, resulting in the remaining Sn1.8Ag solder matrix after electromigration. The predominant (Cu,Ni)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> IMC was formed at the interfaces, preventing the undesirable Kirkendall void formation in the CU<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn phase. The polarity effect occurred in the solder interconnects with a thicker IMC on the anode side. The additional incorporation of Ag metallization at the Sn1.8Ag/Cu lead frame interface and the subsequent Ag3Sn IMC formation have a limited effect on suppressing interdiffusion and inhibiting the formation of CU<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sn IMCs on the Cu pillar or Cu lead frame side, regardless of the electron flow direction. The results presented in this study offer insights for optimizing solder interconnect design by selecting appropriate metallization combinations to mitigate electromigration-induced failures.

articleTitle: Advanced Optical Metrology Using on Surface Morphology Characterization of Polyimide for Process Quality Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The surface morphology and stacking topography are significant indicators in high density redistribution layers (RDL) and stacking via layout for advanced packaging development. With the rapid development of AI and HPC, products with fine-pitch RDL (Line/Space < 2/2um) and increasing layers of via stacking have become key drivers of technology innovation. To achieve goals of high density RDL development, the surface morphology characterization of Polyimide (PI) material is needed to develop, and which is important for process capability control. Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) is a common and reliable methodology to be used in measuring surface roughness values of a small area, but it is challenging to measure the entire 12-inch wafer surface performance due to throughput concern. In this paper, we demonstrate a novel metrology called “Advanced Optical Metrology” (AOM) which can provide the whole 12-inch wafer surface morphology information within one minute of measuring time. The AOM can be used to observe the details of the surface variation of wafer. The experimental results of this paper show that each curing cyclization rate of PI exhibits different surface profile. In addition, the lower cyclization rates of PI film after surface treatment are significantly affected than higher cyclization rates under the same chemical treatment conditions. Overall, the demo cases of this paper demonstrate the versatility and usefulness of AOM in analyzing the surface properties of different materials and providing valuable insights into the surface properties of materials, which can be used to optimize surface treatment and curing conditions for various applications.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip Gap Waveguide Based on Dual-Layer UC-EBG Structure (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Microstrip gap waveguide (MGW) has gained the considerable attention due to the low-weight, low loss, and low-profile structure to replace the conventional metallic hollow rectangular waveguide and microstrip lines at millimeter-wave applications. Electromagnetic band gap (EBG) has been utilized to act as high impedance surface to suppress the surface waves on the dielectric substrate and to reflect the incident wave with zero phase reflection in high frequency applications. Recently, the uniplanar compact electromagnetic band gap (UC-EBG) has gain great attention due to its compactness, low profile, and ease of fabrication rather than mushroom-type EBG. The periodic texture patterns can be designed and fabricated as artificially magnetic conductor (AMC) printed on thin organic substrate to form a dual-layer UC-EBG. An Inverted microstrip gap waveguide (IMGW) is stacked on the top of the proposed dual-layer UC-EBG. This proposed IMGW based on the dual-layer UC-EBG can be considered as an air-gap sandwiched parallel plate waveguide composed of a top metal plate and a grounded textured substrate with two AMC sidewalls confinement. When a separation of an AMC and a top metal plate as parallel perfect conductor (PEC) is smaller than one-quarter wavelength, this air-filled IMGW produces a stopband prohibiting all the specific electromagnetic waveguide modes propagating between AMC and PEC parallel plate except for the quasi-TEM mode along the microstrip line. Dual-layer UC-EBG has wider stopband ranges than single-layer UC-EBG made with the same substrate material. This paper first presents the structure and design parameters of a dual layer UC-EBG and the dispersion characteristics of dual layer UC-EBG is analyzed by the commercial simulation software. Then, an air-filled IMGW based on dual-layer UC-EBG is proposed and its characteristic impedance and transmission and reflection coefficients are further presented.

articleTitle: Productivity Enhancement in Semiconductor Manufacturing with Ai-Enabled Operations Digital Twin Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: There is a significant need to optimize human-machine collaboration in electronics manufacturing, where high labor and equipment costs make downtimes costly. Although digital twins offer promising opportunities, only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$26 \%$</tex> of companies have made substantial progress in their initiatives. This paper presents an AI-enabled operations digital twin platform that digitizes operator activities and integrates them with machine and other factory data to create a comprehensive digital replica of manufacturing processes. Utilizing radar, computer vision, and sensor fusion on the edge, the system enables precise indoor tracking without the need for wearable tags. The combination of digitized activity and factory operations data is then analyzed using AI to generate actionable insights about adverse operational events such as downtimes and their root-causes Deployed in several semiconductor and electronics manufacturing companies, the platform has been used to identify opportunities to significantly improve production efficiency, reduce downtimes, and minimize operational variability. These results underscore the importance of incorporating operator data for optimal manufacturing operations.

articleTitle: Research on the Crystallinity of Metal Passivation Layer for Improving Low-Temperature Copper Bonding Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The study of copper bonding for hybrid bonding is crucial for high-performance devices; however, copper, which is easily oxidized, faces challenges in low-temperature bonding. Metal passivation of copper bonding has emerged as an appropriate solution to address these issues. This research compares the properties of metal passivation layers (titanium, platinum, tantalum, chromium) that protect the copper layer from native oxidation, and investigates their diffusion behavior and the underlying causes. The effects of copper diffusion on grain size and surface roughness are compared, along with the identification of additional factors. It was found that the crystallinity of the metal passivation layer aligns more closely with the trends in diffusion behavior than grain size and surface roughness. The interfaces after the actual bonding process were examined for metal passivation specimens with different crystallinities. Differences in diffusion behavior based on crystallinity were consistent with XPS results across various conditions, including bonding temperature, ramp-up, and pressure. Further experiments were conducted to investigate the influence of crystallinity on diffusion behavior in greater detail. The deposition methods were varied to alter the crystallinity of the passivation metals, and factors including grain size and surface roughness were compared. Additionally, bonding and diffusion experiments were performed to observe the behavior. This research aims to enhance the understanding of copper bonding and is expected to positively influence advanced packaging applications such as hybrid bonding.

articleTitle: Integrated Delta-Sigma Modulator with Low Pass Filter for Acoustical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The proposed integrated low pass delta-sigma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Sigma\Delta)$</tex> modulator with low pass filter has been presented and fabricated in CMOS 0.18um processing. Cascaded integrators approach with feedback as well as distributed input coupling (CIFB) topology erase a summation amplifier and achieve low power dissipation. Bilinear implementation technique is designed by switching capacitors with neural network (NN) and applied to the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order elliptic switched-capacitor (SC) loop filter. Experimental results of integrated delta-sigma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Sigma\Delta)$</tex> modulator with low pass filter exhibit performances of acoustics with the proposed earphone and microphone at anechoic chamber room.

articleTitle: Fan-out RDL Packaging Process and Shuttle Service
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the rapid development of AI technology, AI chips have become a cornerstone of high-end technological applications. Various related products are actively exploring ways to integrate AI technology. A hallmark of innovative products and startups is their need for diverse, small-batch manufacturing. To assist the semiconductor industry in tapping into this highly innovative market, it is essential to develop new small-batch production models. We aim to provide a shuttle service through our innovative platform, significantly reducing the cost and time for developing new products through shared services. This service model allows startups and innovative products to experiment and improve at lower costs and faster speeds, thereby reaching the market quicker and standing out in a competitive environment.

articleTitle: Approaches to Streamline Manufacturing in Flexible Hybrid Printed Electronics (FHPE)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Flexible Hybrid Printed Electronics (FHPE) offer significant advantages over traditional Printed Circuit Boards (PCB) and Flexible Printed Circuits (FPC). Conductive circuits are fabricated using additive printing techniques, which directly deposit conductive materials to interconnect components. This approach provides enhanced design flexibility, reduces manufacturing complexity, and offers better compatibility with unconventional substrates, making it ideal for wearable and bio-integrated applications. In this study, we introduce an innovative bridge technology, hereafter referred to as Bridgetech, that revolutionizes the design stage to significantly streamline the manufacturing process. With Bridgetech, the production of 3-layer metal circuit FPCs is reduced from nearly 30 processes to just one-third. This approach also addresses issues related to excessive thickness and flatness in multilayer metal stacking. Not only does it lower costs and technical complexities, but it also supports ESG goals by minimizing environmental impact and improving resource efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced PCI Express Receiver Channel Signal Quality Validation for AI Server
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this study, we present an enhanced methodology for evaluating the signal quality of PCI Express receiver channels. Our approach incorporates the use of a PCIe Riser equipped with various loss boards, enabling the simulate the scenario of different channel lengths and loss conditions. This innovative addition facilitates the fine-tuning of the test environment to reflect a range of trace loss scenarios, thereby providing a more robust assessment of signal integrity. The methodology leverages an advanced RX Eye Diagram analysis to accurately gauge the signal quality. By examining the Eye Height and Eye Width metrics, we can track the trend of the eye size, which serves as a reliable indicator of the receiver channel's performance and robustness. The integration of the PCIe Riser into our testing framework allows for a detailed understanding of the channel's behavior, supporting targeted design improvements. Overall, our proposed methodology offers a comprehensive tool for the precise evaluation and optimization of PCI Express receiver channels, ensuring enhanced signal quality and system reliability.

articleTitle: Warpage Analysis of Thermo-compression Bonding on Coreless Substrates (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Thermo-compression bonding (TCB) technology has been used in flip chip (FC) package for high volume manufacturing especially in advanced heterogeneous integration packaging. FC package provides the advantages of lower profile, higher inputs/outputs, and higher electrical performance demanded in the high frequency/speed and great bandwidth of high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) applications. To meet these requirements, a coreless substrate is also employed in the FC package by the TCB process to achieve high electrical performance and multiple function of module, such as CoWoS (Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate). Similar advanced package or module like as CoWoS or FOCoS (Fan-Out Chip on Substrate) has been presented and utilized with coreless substrate in recent years. Thermal warpage issues due to mismatch of thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) in various package materials are seriously encountered. In this paper, thermal warpage analyses of a large die bonded on coreless substrate under TCB process are presented. These analyses are simulated and measured by shadow moiré. Method of improving the vacuum mechanism of the bond stage to suppress the warpage of coreless substrate is also proposed.

articleTitle: Estimating Warpage of Fan-Out Panel-Level Packages Under Different Manufacturing Processes Using a Viscoplastic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of technology and the increasing market demand, large-area production has become a goal; fan-out panel-level packaging(FO-PLP) has been selected as a solution to these challenges. However, during the process, mismatches in the coefficients of thermal expansion between different materials can lead to substantial warpage behavior, reducing the reliability and yield of the packaging. This study establishes a 320mm x 320mm three-dimensional(3D) model using the Finite Element Method (FEM) combined with Process Modeling technology to analyze the warpage behavior in FO-PLP during the process, including the effects of different temperature loads during compression molding, Post Mold Cure (PMC) and debonding processes. Epoxy molding compound, used as a protective structure in the packaging, is discussed and compared to the viscoelastic and viscoplastic models. The viscoelastic model considers time-dependent mechanical properties and elastic recovery, effectively describing the deformation behavior of the epoxy molding compound. However, the viscoplastic model is more suitable for accurately predicting the behavior of real materials. To verify the feasibility of the epoxy resin viscoplastic material model, this study conducts numerical validation with experimental test vehicles. By constructing a large panel model consistent with the experimental dimensions and specific temperature load conditions, warpage values are predicted and compared with experimental values, achieving good matching results. This establishes the usability of the viscoplastic model for subsequent use.

articleTitle: Performance and Power Analysis on Immersion Cooling Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper will focus on the immersion cooling heatsinks performance and system power efficiency analysis through test measured data of different key design considerations including different CPU heatsinks, TIM2 (Thermal Interface Material) materials and immersion coolants at different flow rates. In order to collect the immersion cooling system power and heatsinks performance data, three immersion cooling levels tests including component level, server system level and immersion tank level have been performed. This paper has compared the server system power saving under immersion cooling and air cooling and different heatsinks performance with different TIM2 materials under immersion cooling environment. The key single phase immersion cooling design considerations are CPU heatsink thermal solution design, TIM2 selection. Two types of different liquid as Fluorinert FC-40 and Hydrocarbon PAO6 are selected to compare the thermal performance in component and system level test. Test results have shown CPU heatsink thermal solution selection priority as EVAC > Cu Fin> Al Fin> AL-Extrusion on 1 U/2U server adoption in the single-phase immersion cooling, and FC-40 has better power efficiency compared with PAO6. Finally, tank level thermal test is performed at different flow rates and liquid inlet temperature with results showing 12%~34% power saving compared with air cooling. It is concluded that better thermal performance and power efficiency for immersion cooling compared with air cooling based on the data analysis. These performance and power saving data analysis will help designers to improve the immersion cooling server system power efficiency and design better performance system with cost effective. Furthermore, the adoption of these immersion cooling design solutions in this paper can also be scaled out to the high-power CPU of the near future platforms on Intel products roadmap.

articleTitle: 3D Stress Mapping in Processed SiC Wafers by Hyperspectral Raman Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We used confocal hyperspectral Raman imaging to explore Raman spectroscopy to characterize residual stress due to fracture in SiC wafers. This was done by focusing on the peak at 776 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, which is related to local residual stress By combining the information from the Raman and SEM images, we could show that the stress, due to fraction of the substrate, propagates all up to the surface of the substrate and even into the epitaxial layer, without the need for any sample preparation.

articleTitle: A Novel Polymer Material for Low- Temperature Hybrid Bonding and Flexible Substrate Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As transistor density increases, 3D integrated circuits and advanced packaging technologies are crucial for extending Moore's Law. Traditional polymer material challenges include such as warpage in organic interposers with multiple redistribution layers (RDLs) and reliability issues due to mismatches in the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). To address these issues, a novel polymer material has been developed. This material not only has a low CTE but also exhibits a higher Young's modulus compared to other polymers, making it highly promising for flexible substrate applications. The polymer was used for room-temperature bonding, combining ultra-thin glass (UTG) with polyimide (PI), and then was subjected to a 200,000-cycle bending test. The results demonstrated excellent flexibility and stability of the composite polymer structure on flexible substrates. In addition, the polymer was applied in low-temperature copper/polymer hybrid bonding, achieving reliable bonding at 160°C, and its electrical performance and high reliability were confirmed through thermal cycling tests (TCT). These findings underscore the potential of this polymer in flexible substrate and hybrid bonding applications, providing a practical and effective solution for achieving superior bonding and electrical performance at reduced temperatures.

articleTitle: Cable Bending Impact to High-Speed SERDES
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: PAM4 modulation such as PCIE6 link is prone to voltage noises due to reduction on signal to noise ratio to 9.6dB relative to NRZ signaling. One of the biggest contributors to voltage degradation is due to signal reflection at interconnect and mode-conversion cause by imbalanced in channel properties such as impedance variations and delay. This paper investigates intra-pair skew due to cable bending empirically using lab measurements. Firstly, the main concern for cable skew is on common-to-differential mode conversion since it will add as noise at differential receiver. Our studies indicated a small increase of Sdc21by 3dB for different bending cases compared to baseline thus alleviated the concerns of increase Sdc21 cause by cable bending. Secondly, excessive cable bending can cause damage or change of electrical properties such as characteristic impedance and propagation delay. Our studies indicated cable bending cause small impedance discontinuities of 1 to 2-ohm at locality of the bending. This studies also suggest cable impedance variations at location of bending to be modelled into end-end simulation. We also observed negligible differential propagation delay variations of <1 ps for all four cases. Effective intra-pair skew (EIPS) is also <3ps which is within PCIe Gen6 cable requirements. Simulations suggested negligible impact to margins since the cable impedance and skew variations are still within the expected high-volume manufacturing (HVM) variations and tolerances. These studies suggest there are possibility to bend cable beyond cable manufacture recommendation in a very tight system yet still passing the performance requirement. However, it is advice for system architect to work closely with cable vendor on mechanical and reliability risks. Cable vendor may have options to recommend a different option such as cable jackets reinforcement or other options.

articleTitle: Developing Pad Design Rule for Wafer-Level Package Through Pad Size Effect Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Solder joint fatigue is a common failure in wafer-level packages (WLP) under thermal cycling loads, caused by the expansion and contraction of materials with different thermal expansion coefficients. This leads to crack formation and electrical failures. In WLP design, the dimensions of upper and lower copper pads influence the shape, height, and angle of solder balls, affecting their contact area, mechanical support, and stress distribution. These factors determine the stability and reliability of solder joints during long-term thermal cycling, impacting the overall reliability of the package. In this study, we will use different sizes of upper and lower copper pads in multiple test vehicles to observe their impact on performance and reliability. Due to the time-intensive nature of evaluating multiple vehicles, full adoption of three-dimensional (3D) modeling methods is impractical. Instead, we will employ 3D models to validate the accuracy of two-dimensional (2D) models and establish optimal design criteria based on insights from 2D simulations. This study identifies the expected optimal design criteria through successfully validated 2D models, aiming to use the finite element method (FEM) to simulate reliability tests, reducing testing time and revealing potential failure mechanisms for design improvement. In WLP design, different sizes of upper and lower copper pads affect the solder balls' shape, height, and angle, thereby influencing their mechanical support and thermal stress distribution. By observing the impact of these variations on performance and reliability in different test vehicles, we ultimately establish cost-effective and reliable optimal packaging design standards.

articleTitle: Warpage and Stress Analysis in Molded 2.5D Package Chiplet Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the slowing of Moore's Law, chiplet technology emerges as a cost-effective and scalable solution to the challenges of advancing semiconductor manufacturing. It allows for the integration of heterogeneous chiplets, each designed under optimal process technology nodes, to meet specific application requirements. 2.5D silicon interposer packaging platform has been widely used in heterogeneous chiplet integrated packaging to support high-end performance product requirements. In this study, we focused on2.5D package to evaluate structural and material solution at initial design stage. In this work, numerical FE models of molded 2.5D package was built-up. Simulations of different design of combo die layout configuration and interposer thickness were performed to assess warpage and ILD stress. The simulations demonstrated that the four smaller ASIC dies were combined into a single die or reduces interposer thickness could reduce the package warpage. However, they would exist combo die warpage and ILD stress risk. Key effects of different material properties are also performed through simulation analysis. The simulation results show that adjusting the mechanical properties of EMC and WUF could effectively reduce ILD stress and early-stage combo die warpage, positively impacting the reliability of the package. However, it has limited influence on the final package warpage. Future improvements could combine material adjustments with structural changes for a more comprehensive approach to minimizing both warpage and stress. Through optimization analysis, subsequently, a design guideline will be established based on the simulation results to facilitate future designs for molded 2.5D package chiplet integration.

articleTitle: Driving Efficiency and Reliability in AI Hardware: Leading Edge Pulse Plating Solutions for Uniform Copper Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The rapid expansion of the artificial intelligence (AI) market has created an urgent demand for innovative and efficient solutions in the manufacturing of integrated circuit (IC) substrates. A critical aspect of IC-substrate production is electrolytic copper plating, essential for ensuring electrical conductivity, reliability, and overall performance of the circuits. Traditional copper plating techniques often face challenges in achieving uniform deposition and adequate copper thickness in through-holes, which are crucial for high-performance AI applications. This paper explores recent advancements in electrolytic copper plating technologies, focusing on the application of pulse plating in vertical conveyorized equipment to address these challenges and deliver superior results.

articleTitle: 3D PSF Deconvolution to Enhance Optical Critical Dimension Measurement and Extend Effective Depth-of-Focus in Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study presents a novel parameterized three-dimensional Point Spread Function (3D PSF) model utilizing the Zernike aberration model to address optical aberrations in critical dimension (CD) metrology for brightfield microscopy. Traditional high numerical aperture objectives enhance lateral resolution but suffer from limited depth of focus, complicating accurate 3D imaging. Our integrated optical and computational approach employs 3D PSF deconvolution to effectively compensate for optical system limitations, resulting in clearer and more precise 3D images. The proposed method successfully doubles the depth of focus compared to conventional systems. Validation through CD measurements demonstrated a 50% reduction in measured bias errors within the initial depth of focus range and a decrease from over 8.53% to 1.05% in the extended range of 1 to 2 times the original focus depth. These improvements are significant for precision engineering applications, particularly in semiconductor manufacturing, enhancing process variation management and yield rates.

articleTitle: Variable Switching Frequency Global Driving Strategy of SiC-MOSFET and Si-IGBT-based Motor Drive System for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study introduces a variable switching frequency (VSF) global control strategy to improve the output current quality and efficiency of an electric vehicle drive system. Using Matlab/Simulink, the motor and controller system are simulated to automatically identify the optimal switching frequency for various operating points. Once the optimal switching frequency lookup table is generated offline, it can be used in the drive system to ensure an optimal balance between efficiency and current quality across all global operating points. Additionally, this study models both Si IGBT and SiC MOSFET modules from Infineon, revealing that SiC MOSFETs have lower switching losses compared to Si IGBTs, making them a great choice for high efficiency electric vehicle application. Overall, the built model is suitable for power loss analysis in the early stages of development, and a VSF strategy is proposed for determining optimal switching frequency. These results establish a solid foundation for efficiency improvements in motor drive systems.

articleTitle: Characterization of PVD SiCN dielectric for Hybrid Bonding Application
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: SiCN has gained attention as a dielectric material in hybrid bonding due to its excellent surface roughness after chemical mechanical polishing, copper diffusion barrier properties, and high bonding strength. Typically, SiCN deposition is carried out using plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), which involves high deposition and annealing temperatures exceeding 350°C. In this study, we investigate the potential of SiCN as a dielectric material for hybrid bonding by depositing it using physical vapor deposition (PVD). The PVD SiCN process is less complicated than the PECVD SiCN process and the deposition temperature is also lower. To evaluate PVD SiCN films, the effects of RF power and the Ar/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ratio on the films were investigated. The deposition rate ranged from a minimum of 124.5 Å/min to a maximum of 428.3 Å/min, depending on the process conditions. The oxygen content in the SiCN thin films varied between 11% and 65% based on the deposition conditions, and the refractive index ranged from 1.5 to 1.9.

articleTitle: Development of High Heat Dissipation Thermosetting Sintering Cu Paste
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: According to the rapid demand expansion of generative AI, to improve turning to higher density and integration in 2.XD and 3D packages that mounting CPU and GPU. We think the high density and integration cause thermal problem with each device. As the countermeasures, they use thermal interface material (TIM) 1 which embeds between the Si chip and lid, and TIM2 which embeds between the lid and heat sink, is used mainly by TIM sheets that contain graphite.
