articleTitle: Advanced Development of Embedded Technology on Ceramic Embedded Laminate (CEL) Structure for Thermal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the advent of the 5G, 6G, and AI generations, the power of components themselves is increasing, leading to higher levels of generated heat. Hence, addressing the issue of temperature-induced damage to components is urgent. Embedded technology emerged early on to address heat dissipation issues, and today it boasts unique design advantages in various applications. Among them, while the essence of embedded ceramic substrates and traditional embedded copper blocks is similar, their different embedded materials result in different technological aspects. This article comprehensively explores the technology of embedded ceramic substrates, elucidating their principles, applications, and advantages. Firstly, this article delves into the manufacturing process of embedded ceramic substrate PCBs, outlining the steps involved in embedding ceramic substrates within PCB boards. The material characteristics of ceramic substrates are starkly different from those of typical PCB materials, making the integration of these two heterogeneous materials a focal point of this study. Therefore, in addition to discussing the materials and techniques used to achieve this integration, the importance of precision placement and consistency between layers is also emphasized. Furthermore, this article elucidates the advantages of embedded ceramic substrate technology. These include excellent thermal conductivity and the reduction in size and weight due to decreased copper thickness. Moreover, embedded ceramic substrate PCBs benefit from the insulation properties of ceramic substrates themselves, enabling the integration with PCB boards and allowing for co-design of circuits, thus reducing losses in layout area. The article also discusses the diverse applications of embedded ceramic substrate PCBs in industries such as high-power electronics, automotive systems, and industrial control. Additionally, it addresses how to tackle specific challenges in these areas, including heat dissipation, circuit design, and space constraints. In summary, this article underscores the transformative potential of embedded ceramic substrate technology in the PCB field and highlights the differences from embedded copper blocks. By directly embedding ceramic substrates into PCB materials, this technique offers an alternative solution to the evolving heat dissipation needs of modern electronic products, thereby enabling higher performance and miniaturization of electronic systems.

articleTitle: Predicting Wrinkle Formation in Flexible Thin-Film Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Flexible microsystems and packages frequently contain thin-film structures attached to a compliant substrate. Surface wrinkles driven by deformation instability may develop, either as an unwanted feature, or it may actually be created by design to enhance certain functionalities. Conventional numerical modeling of wrinkling instabilities typically involves an artificial multi-step process. In this paper we present a modeling methodology capable of predicting the initiation and temporal evolution of surface wrinkles in a straightforward fashion. In addition to the planar structure of a thin film on a flat substrate under in-plane uniaxial and equi-biaxial compressions, the film/substrate system in a cylindrical fiber form under axial loading is also considered. In the pure linear elastic state, the simulation results may be verified by available analytical solutions. We further extend the modeling to include plastic yielding of the film material, leading to transformation of periodic wrinkles into more severe forms of permanent folds.

articleTitle: Automatically Generate SMT Mounter Production Data with Python Web Scraping
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study proposes an automated data collection method that combines web scraping and production data storage web pages to improve the efficiency of data production for SMT production metrics. It focuses on extracting data from Panasonic's “Proviewer” webpages and generating data on the Mounters' Line Balance Rate and Loss Rate. After confirming with the vendor that using web scrapping for USI's internal data collection does not cause copyright infringement, Python's Selenium and BeautifulSoup packages were implemented. This automated the traditional manual data collection and measurement methods of the IE and PD departments, capturing data directly from the platform and presenting it visually with statistical verification. The ultimate goal is not only to automate the generation of metrics but also to reduce the workload of counterparts through programming language assistance.

articleTitle: Mature Defect-Free Micro Processing for Advanced IC Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The semiconductor industry is constantly evolving, driven by the demand for higher performance, greater miniaturization, and increased integration density in electronic devices. Traditional organic and ceramic substrates, while effective, are increasingly challenged by the requirements of modern high-performance applications such as AI and high-performance computing (HPC). Glass substrates have emerged as a promising alternative due to their superior thermal stability, electrical performance, and mechanical strength. However, the brittleness of glass and its susceptibility to defects have historically limited its use in high-volume semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Electrical Characterization and Testing of BGA Gripper-Type Socket for High-Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Ball Grid Array packaging technology has become a viable option in today's high-speed integrated circuit design, where utilizing a BGA socket is essential in high-performance applications. This paper discusses the electrical characteristics and testing of a single-sided gripper-type pin socket technology. Due to the irregular shape and discontinuities of the gripper socket pin, it has become very compelling to study the signal integrity effect for this socket pin technology and its suitability in multi-Giga Hertz applications. The gripper-type socket was modeled and characterized at higher frequencies for multi-ports single-ended and differential configurations. To achieve this, 3D numerical simulations were performed using the HFSS FEM model from Ansoft Corporation. The S-parameters of the socket pin with 0.5-mm pitch testing configuration were evaluated up to 40 GHz. In addition, the insertion and return loss of single-ended and differential configurations were characterized at frequencies of 5 and 10 GHz. Furthermore, Real- time functional testing was conducted to perform read-and-write operations using an embedded Multimedia Card (eMMC) memory grippe socket platform.

articleTitle: Impact of Electrical Current Stressing on η'-Cu6Sn5 in Electronics Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In advanced electronic packaging, the stability of intermetallic compounds (IMCs) under high electric current density is crucial for the reliability of solder joints. Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>, a predominant IMC formed between Sn-based solders and Cu substrates, exists in two allotropes: the high-temperature hexagonal phase and the low-temperature monoclinic η' phase, with a transition temperature of 186°C. This study investigates the effects of electric current on η'-Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> phase, focusing on structural characterization and mechanical properties. Various electric current densities were applied to thermally aged η'-Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>. Synchrotron radiation-based X-ray diffraction (SR-XRD) was used to examine crystallographic changes, while nanoindentation tests assessed mechanical property alterations. These observations contribute to understanding the impact of electric current density on the structural and mechanical behavior of the monoclinic η'-Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> phase.

articleTitle: A Reliable and Scalable nPI-based Statistical Methodology for Post-Silicon IO Testing and Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Reliable testing of systems is one of the critical milestones in the overall product launch process. As industry expands, deployment of systems over a vast field of applications includes high safety use-cases beyond just data centers. The quality of testing and improved reliability has been the top priority combined with meeting time-to-market schedules. In this paper, we will present a robust and scalable solution of defining the base test criteria using the statistical concept of prediction interval over future ‘n’ observations (nPI). We will present key indicators that make the proposal a reliable solution to apply across various protocols of SerDes and memory.

articleTitle: Advanced Solder Dispensing Process Evaluation for Miniaturization and 3D Assembly (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The benefit of Miniaturization technology is obviously, providing product smaller XYZ size to accommodate larger volume battery to increase battery life of terminal product or integrating more functions (components) within original layout area. Not only be applied on SiP module but also PCBA, especially for mobile (phone/Laptop/Tablet…) and wearable devices (earphone/smart watch/smart glasses…). Solder dispensing process is widely applied on metal shield soldering in SiP module in USI. Advanced solder dispenser can dispense extremely small dot size which is smaller than 100um to provide the required solder paste for tiny components, for example passive 008004” and fine pitch (< 200 um) bump package. It is valuable especially on mixed component size(big and fine pitch) layout case. 3D assembly (cavity design) is another applied case, not only fabrication cost and lead time of 3D stencil is much higher (~2 times) than a normal one, but also lifecycle is also a concern. The purpose of this paper is to evaluate an advanced solder paste dispenser and alternative solder paste models to get engineering ready for miniaturization and 3D SMT assembly solution in the future.

articleTitle: Advanced Electroplating Processes for IC Substrates - Redistribution Layer and Embedded Trenches
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The rapid developments in the electronics sector have increasingly merged the worlds of printed circuit boards (PCB) and integrated circuit (IC) substrates/semiconductors. This fusion is anchored by the IC substrate, which forms the critical link between IC chips and PCBs, utilizing a network of conductive copper (Cu) traces and vias for connectivity. The advanced IC substrate market is expected to double to $34 billion by 2028, being propelled by the increasing complexity of electronic devices, driven by advancements in GPUs, AI accelerators, and cloud computing technologies. This growth is further amplified by over $15 billion in investments since 2021, reflecting the sector's dynamic potential and the strategic emphasis on high-density connectivity solutions. IC substrates are at the forefront of the electronics industry's drive towards greater miniaturization, higher yield, and lower costs. The quest for minimizing the distance between Cu traces to achieve maximum substrate utilization underscores the industry's push towards advanced wafer-level technologies with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 2\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> line and space (L/S) with strict uniformity within unit (WIU) and within panel (WIP). The emerging challenges and opportunities presented by scale mismatch and smaller L/S distances necessitate innovations like fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP). The development of new plating solutions, focusing on uniformity and planarity, is crucial for overcoming the hurdles in multilayer processing, preventing signal transmission loss, and ensuring the reliability of increasingly complex electronic systems. The integration of cutting-edge additive packages for DC Cu electroplating, emphasizing trench and via filling capabilities, exemplifies the industry's commitment to pushing the boundaries of IC substrate technology, paving the way for the next generation of electronics manufacturing.

articleTitle: System Level Heat Sink Design of Power Module for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Thermal management is crucial for EV/HEV applications, as it significantly impacts both output performance and system reliability. To enhance thermal performance, the heat sink design of the power module must be improved. Additionally, system performance can be predicted using electrical circuit simulations. The power loss during inverter operation can be estimated based on the electrical characteristics of the power module, which vary with junction temperature. This study focuses on the thermal design of a silicon carbide (SiC) power module equipped with an innovative wavy fin heat sink for inverter applications. The system under analysis is a 55 kW inverter featuring a 1200 V, 400 A SiC power module. Initially, the thermal performance of the wavy fin heat sink is predicted through computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation. Subsequently, system performance is simulated by coupling electrical and thermal models using PSIM software. A comprehensive analysis of output current, junction temperature, and power loss during system operation is then conducted.

articleTitle: In-Situ Condition Monitoring of SiC-MOSFETs During Active Power Cycling Using Acoustic Emission Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper analyses the potentials of acoustic emission testing during active power cycling of SiC-MOSFETs. For the first time, it can be shown that the acoustic measurements provide meaningful insight into the health status of fully-encapsulated SiC-MOSFETs during lifetime testing. This noninvasive testing method shows wear-out much prior to the conventional failure criterion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{DS}}$</tex> -increase.

articleTitle: Elimination of Ti Residue Caused Yield Loss for Panel Level Package
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This case study demonstrates application of a problem solving methodology that consists of define, measure, analyze, improve, and control (DMAIC) phases. During early development phase of ultra-large scale panel level package (PLP), Titanium (Ti) residue related yield loss was observed in automatic optical inspection (AOI). Ti etch non-uniformity (primarily at edges of ultra-large panels), Ti etching shielding due to deposition of etching byproducts onto upper electrode cover of plasma chamber, and bias in XRF (X-ray Fluorescence) measurements of Ti thickness were identified as key reasons for Ti residue related yield losses. Application of elimination-DMAIC methodology enabled to investigate and drive improvements for achieving elimination of Ti residue related yield losses.

articleTitle: RSM Methodology for Accuracy Enhancement In SerDes Channel Solution Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: System hardware design solution cost is one of the key factors for product Average Selling Price (ASP), which directly impacts revenue and profit margins. A hardware design solution with a higher cost compared to a competitor's design might incur the risk of a product selling price rebate or being turned down altogether by a customer. The PCIe Gen 5 application is an important variable that can result in an additional 20% of total system build of material (BOM) through printed circuit board (PCB) material selection and additional placement of re-timer per PCIe Gen 5 port. A poorly designed system might incur such additional costs despite not having to. The ability of a highly correlated simulation methodology to predict a feasible routing solution through pre-silicon simulation on platform topologies with high confidence is therefore critical. It helps design engineers push the boundary on the hardware design solution and make necessary trade-offs in the design solution on PCB material, rather than complicate the design with additional re-timers. This paper proposes a Response Surface Modeling (RSM) technique in conjunction with the Design of Experiment (DOE) as an accurate statistical Signal Integrity (SI) analysis methodology. This enables platform designers to design cost-effective and healthy systems throughout product development by performing reliable SI trade-off analyses.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Study on the Global Analysis of New Multimodal Optical Metrology for Critical Dimension (CD) Measurement and Stress Analysis in Advanced Semiconductor Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study focuses on simulating and theoretically analyzing a multimodal approach to new optical metrology, utilizing Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) and Finite Element Modeling (FEM) to determine the critical dimension (CD) and thermo-mechanical stress of high aspect ratio through silicon via (TSV) components. Global parameter sensitivity analysis is crucial for optimizing the metrology methodology and the optical measurement system. The proposed system methodology can measure CDs and stress, enabling real-time, in-line monitoring and control essential for maintaining high yields in semiconductor manufacturing. Deep ultraviolet (DUV) scatterometry measures high aspect ratio TSV CDs, as DUV light penetrates TSV structures. The FDTD simulation and global sensitivity analysis evaluate optical response variations due to Depth, TCD, BCD, and Spacing changes. Optimizing the illumination settings enhances the accuracy of sensitivity analysis. Depth is higher sensitive, and Spacing is lower sensitive. The higher tilt angle of 20° of illumination settings makes TCD, BCD, and Spacing more sensitive. Besides, mechanical stress in fine-pitch packaging deforms TSV structures, causing defects and device failure. This study uses 3D FEM to analyze stress tensors around copper-filled TSVs, ensuring reliable thermal stress determination. The overall stress distribution within the sample varies from -200 MPa to 800 MPa. A correlation is observed between the stress in silicon and the Raman frequency shift, which ranges from -4.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> to 2.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and is associated with the inelastic scattering of incident electromagnetic waves. This multimodal approach advances the system for inline stress and CD metrology.

articleTitle: Study of Solder Resist Undercut for Flip Chip Chip Scale Package Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The product trend of FCCSP is that line width and line space are getting smaller and smaller. As the line space shrinks, we found that the short defect which causing by copper dendrite tend to happen at solder resist undercut area of bump on line product, and is correlated with the solder resist undercut length and trace space. Under normal circumstances, chemical residue tends to happen at solder resist undercut area due to clean method limitation, and after absorbing steam it become an environment suitable for copper dendrite growth. So as solder resist undercut length reduces, the happen chance of chemical residue would drop together, which means short defect causing by copper dendrite would drop, too. Therefore, this article discusses the relationship between trace space and solder resist undercut through the DOE of line space. (Solder resist undercut: Following present by abbreviation SRU)

articleTitle: Characterization and Optimization of SiCN Films for Low-Temperature Cu Hybrid Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As Moore's Law approaches its physical limits, this study explores SiCN's potential as a superior alternative to SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> for low-temperature hybrid bonding in 3D integration. We analyze SiCN films deposited at 180°C and 350°C to achieve defect-free interfaces comparable to those in higher-temperature processes. This helps reduce the thermal budget and prevent device degradation. Additionally, we employ O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma treatments to lower the bonding temperature to 180°C further. The research ultimately aims to establish SiCN-SiCN low-temperature hybrid bonding as a viable and effective solution for next-generation semiconductor applications.

articleTitle: Electroless Plating of ENEPIG and EPAG – Comparing the Impact of Pd-Bath Type and Au-Bath Type on the Deposit Properties and Manufacturing Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: For high performance and high reliability applications like they are present in the HDI or IC substrate industry, the final finish Ni/Pd/Au, also known as ENEPIG (Electroless Nickel, Electroless Palladium, Immersion Gold) is well-established. It provides a high solder joint integrity and is wire bondable with different types of metal wires. For some years already the nickel free surface finishes Pd/Au or Au/Pd/Au are considered as potential alternatives when it comes to shrinking feature sizes, smaller lines and spaces or high frequency applications where nickel is considered as limitation. This paper focuses on key differences and similarities of Pure Pd and PdP-type ENEPIG layers as well as different types of gold electrolytes with immersion or autocatalytic dominated reaction mechanism. The study is split into three sections with the first focusing on the PdP vs. Pure Pd ENEPIG comparison, the second on the gold bath evaluation and the third on the comparison of Pd/Au vs. ENEPIG. In section one the comparison of different palladium plating solutions includes the study of the initial plating reaction of Pure Pd vs. PdP plating electrolytes and the performance related to background and excessive plating. It is shown, that depending on the type of electrolyte different sensitivity towards process contamination is observed which affects the deposition reaction. The palladium electrolytes are also compared in bath composition and Pd-content and the resulting effect on the cost contribution to plating process cost. Real data from mass production environment are compared with cost estimations backing up the estimated savings of a modified Pd-plating process. In the second part, the type of gold electrolyte and plating mechanism are studied to compare the impact on plating homogeneity and achievable layer thickness. The plating mechanism for immersion and autocatalytic gold electrolytes are described and solutions are presented to prevent the additional usage of potassium cyanide for stabilization. In the final section certain perspectives of the final finish Pd/Au are compared to ENEPIG looking in particular into the capabilities in the solder joint integrity and the signal loss in high frequency applications. Beside that, different aspects of the required production environment and equipment are highlighted which is needed to implement ENEPIG or Pd/Au plating capabilities at a PCB manufacturing plant. The paper gives insights into the potential solutions for process modification of the well-established final finish ENEPIG to target and fulfill the future demands in HDI and IC substrate manufacturing by widening the plating capabilities.

articleTitle: The Advanced DC Circuit Model for Hybrid bonding in Dual Damascene Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As the miniaturization of devices and advancements in process technology have reached their limits, hybrid bonding has emerged as a new solution for fine-pitch processes in 3D bonding methods. Hybrid bonded structures vary in type and shape depending on the process. It became necessary to develop a new DC circuit model that could accurately capture the magnitude and trends of total resistance in these diverse structures. In particular, we designed a resistance model for structures utilizing the dual damascene process, a new method that allows easy adjustment of resistance and current by controlling the number of vias. Additionally, one of the most important methods for evaluating bonding quality in hybrid bonding is the extraction of contact resistance. This model includes contact resistance in the interface, which provides the necessary information for accurate contact resistance extraction. The accuracy of the SPICE model was measured against FEM simulations based on dimensional analysis. Initially, there was a significant discrepancy between the FEM simulation and the proposed model. However, by incorporating correction factors to compensate for current density bias, we were able to reduce the error to less than 3%, resulting in a highly accurate model.

articleTitle: Advanced Viafill Reliability Using Direct Metallization Technology (IMPACT 2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As technology advances, the need for more difficult and complex board designs continues as well. An increasing number of boards require microvias for functionality with the range of via sizes expanding to span very small and very large vias with wide ranges of aspect ratios. Increased density of vias and finer features have further reduced the line and space requirements to below 25/25 μm. This in turn requires reduced etching during the primary metallization process and new and improved viafill technology. Using a wet etch process, we can reduce the etch rate required in processing to below 1 μm. Further, by studying the interaction between the direct metallization coating and the viafill copper processing, both processes can be optimized to minimize etching, reduce copper budget, and further increase line and space capability. The study was split into two parts: the first to minimize etching required throughout the direct metallization process, and the second to optimize viafill to ensure the thinnest plating copper thickness as possible. We study the conductivity and resistance of the direct metallization layer, allowing us to minimize propagation time and maximize viafill. From there we optimize the viafill chemistry to fill as quickly as possible, reducing copper plating on the surface. Linking the performance of the direct metallization and viafill copper processes allows for a better understanding of the interactions between these two processes and improves the overall performance of the board.

articleTitle: Optimizing PCB Design with Advanced Copper Foil and Superior Oxide Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This study investigates the optimization of PCBs for high-frequency applications by proposed advanced copper foils with ultra-low-loss materials under different oxide treatments. Focusing on minimizing insertion loss, which is crucial for maintaining signal integrity in high-speed interconnects, the research highlights the effectiveness of non-etching treatments for these advanced copper foil. These treatments significantly improve electrical performance by reducing surface roughness and insertion loss, particularly at frequencies of 16GHz and 28GHz. The findings emphasize the importance of selecting appropriate copper treatments to enhance the performance and design flexibility of high-frequency PCBs in datacenter and AI platforms.

articleTitle: TEM Analysis on Nano Defects of Chip Bonding Component Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In the recent years, with the continuous prosperous development, the improvement of integration degree, the complexity of semiconductor chips and the gradual reduced size to the nanoscale of the third-generation semiconductor materials, the requirements for the reliability will also improve, followed by the advances in the failure analysis of chips and structural analysis of more micro materials. On this account, in the field of high-order compound semiconductor chips, it is of vital importance to find the locations of failure points and further analyze the causes for failure. In this research, a new positioning method is developed. Using the combination of known diffraction theory and shooting of planar defect samples, as well as the principle that the bright field images own the maximum image intensity under the double beam diffraction condition, the defect analysis is conducted on the chip planar structure. The detailed morphology of planar structural defects can be visually and clearly observed in TEM, and the cross-sectional samples are further prepared after matching with the following specific positioning of nano defects, further identifying the overall trend and defect source locations of the defects, improving the techniques for common defect analysis and the multi-directional defect trend analysis.

articleTitle: Pioneering the Leading-Edge Adhesion Enhancement System for the Future of Package Substrates Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In microelectronic assembly, the formation of a robust and reliable bond between copper conductor tracks and dielectrics is a must. This necessity becomes even more pronounced in the area of high-density interconnects, where the demand is greater than ever for fine line and space circuitry. The traditional surface roughening processes, that have been relied upon to improve the adhesion of dielectric materials to copper have become impractical. The excessive etching of the conductor tracks has a detrimental effect on their characteristics and signal integrity. With the current challenges in the packaging substrate industry, a novel approach to adhesion improvement is essential. The new process must be independent of surface roughening or etching, have excellent lamination material compatibility and be cost-effective. In this report, a new type of organo-silane adhesion promoter is designed to chemically react with Cu and dielectric materials. It is successfully synthesized in-house with a focus on route optimization, reproducibility, and scale-up. The new promoter improves the initial adhesion strength of ultra-smooth Cu to insulating build up films and prevent loss of adhesion when the substrates are exposed to extremely high temperatures and or/ humid external environments. In addition, the promoter significantly reduces wedge void defects on blind micro vias (BMV) by strengthening the Cu-dielectric interface of patterned substrates against aggressive desmear conditions. High corrosion resistance demonstrated by electrochemical tests. A comparison with a low etch adhesion promoter (LEAP) system will show that the roughness is no longer necessary to ensure a reliable bonding. The newly developed non-roughened solution enables state-of-the-art IC substrate packaging. It also meets the technical specifications of major microprocessor manufacturers.

articleTitle: Plasma Descum on Advanced Packaging Development
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In this study, we have established an automated descum process, and based on MicroWave (MW) plasma system for VIPack advanced semiconductor packaging on underfill treatment process. When the plasma is working, a glow is produced inside the chamber. Experimental results are measured by applying the contact angle method to the treated substrate. The descum process is carried out under optimal chamber vacuum. This experimental result proves that the radio frequency system can ensure that the substrate stably reaches hydrophilic quality during the plasma descum process and can be applied to VIPack advanced packaging.

articleTitle: A Study of a Plating Hanger for a Vertical Copper Electroplating Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 19th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Semiconductor technology plays a crucial role in the advancement of technology. The creation of powerful microchips has made our lives easier by automating tasks, improving communication, and providing access to vast arrays of information. Industries are being transformed through automation and digital innovation. This creates new opportunities and challenges along the way. Semiconductor manufacturers are becoming smarter by constantly improving the processes by which they manufacture and produce these microchips. One effective strategy to increase production and maximize efficiency is to ensure that these machines are regularly maintained and are constantly improved to guarantee the quality and quantity of the products. During the deposition process, the vertical continuous copper electroplating machinery runs nonstop to meet the demands of the manufacturing company. Due to continuous usage, the copper plating hanger's mechanical components encounter unavoidable deformation due to stress and strain, which causes the hanger's components to be misaligned and damaged. In this study, the researcher has redesigned the mechanical components of a copper plating hanger used in vertical continuous copper electroplating machinery, which is a critical piece of machinery utilized in semiconductor manufacturing. The copper plating hanger has three main critical mechanical components, namely the brass conductor, the stainless-steel horizontal bar, and the stainless-steel insulating clips. These components encounter the greatest deformation during continuous usage in the production line, which becomes damaged and unsalvageable after several usages during production; therefore, it is inefficient, unsustainable, and not cost-worthy. Actual mechanical design experiments were conducted to compare the standardized fixed measurements of the copper plating hanger before and after it was used in the production line. The gathered data was used to analyze the misalignments that have occurred after being utilized in the production line. Thereafter, simulations through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) were performed to understand the stress, strain, and displacement behaviors of these components under different parameters and boundary conditions used in the actual design experiments. Comparing results of the aforesaid experiment yielded better design results. Such is useful to develop a more effective and efficient mechanical design. Therefore, design improvements were made for the copper plating hanger following the mechanical design principles from the mechanical engineering discipline. Design improvements were made through the fabrication of newly designed components such as the conductor guide for the brass conductor, the middle bracket for the stainless-steel horizontal bar, and the flange guide for the stainless-steel insulating clips. These newly designed components will improve the stability, precision, and accuracy of the copper plating hanger's three main critical mechanical components, as well as the overall precision of the copper plating hanger, which will contribute to the overall efficiency of the vertical continuous copper electroplating machinery.
